The Planning Team will continue to evaluate and maintain the priorities of each jurisdiction moving forward. 
Currently those priorities are as follows: 
Priorities 
Holbrook 
The City of Holbrook remains committed to efforts to mitigate potential events. The city continues to 
try and balance the competing demands for its limited resources between immediate and long-term 
needs. Section 6.3-6, of the report, includes the tasks that the city is focused on to mitigate potential 
events. 
Pinetop-Lakeside 
The Town of Pinetop-Lakeside’s level of commitment to mitigate potential events has remained unchanged. The 
Town continues to try and balance the competing demands for its limited resources between immediate and 
long-term needs. Section 6.3-3, of the report, includes the tasks that the Town is focused on to mitigate 
potential events. The projects are ranked as high or medium. The tasks include speciﬁc projects (drainage 
improvements) that support certain areas of the Town (Top of the Woods and others).  
Show Low 
The City of Show Low’s level of commitment to mitigate potential events has remained unchanged. The city 
continues to try and balance the competing demands for its limited resources between immediate and long-
term needs. Section 6.3-4, of the report, includes the tasks that the city is focused on to mitigate potential 
events. Some of the tasks address immediate needs (storm water retention enforcement) and others are long-
term needs (surface water treatment plant). 
Snowﬂake 
The Town of Snowﬂake’s level of commitment to mitigate potential events has remained unchanged. The Town 
continues to try and balance the competing demands for its limited resources between immediate and long-
term needs. Section 6.3-5 provides additional details on the tasks that the Town is focused on, ranked by level 
of priority. These tasks are being taken to mitigate potential events. Some of the tasks are completed on a 
regular basis (enforcement of the codes) and one may be completed in the near future (storm drainage 
expansion). 
Taylor 
The Town of Taylor’s level of commitment to mitigate potential events has remained unchanged. The Town 
continues to try and balance the competing demands for its limited resources between immediate and long-
term needs. Section 6.3-6 provides additional details on the tasks that the Town is focused on, ranked by level 
of priority. These tasks are being taken to mitigate potential events. 
Winslow 
The City of Winslow’s level of commitment to mitigate potential events has remained unchanged. The city 
continues to try and balance the competing demands for its limited resources between immediate and long-
term needs. Section 6.3-6, of the report, includes the tasks that the city is focused on to mitigate potential 
events. These tasks include daily and project speciﬁc tasks.

This Plan requires updating and approval from FEMA every ﬁve years. The Plan updates will adhere to that set 
schedule using the following procedure: 
• One year prior to the Plan expiration date, the Planning Team will review and assess the Plan and other 
related documentation. 
• The Planning Team will update and/or revise the appropriate or affected portions of the Plan. 
• The updated Plan will be submitted to DEMA and FEMA for review, comment and approval. 
• Upon receipt of ‘Approvable Pending Adoption’ determination from FEMA, the Planning Team will enter a  
          process by which the jurisdictions’ respective councils officially adopt the Plan. 
• The signed resolutions will be submitted to FEMA to ensure the official approval is received. 
 
7.2  Incorporation into Existing Planning Mechanisms 
Incorporation of the Plan into other planning mechanisms, either by content or reference, enhances a 
community’s ability to perform hazard mitigation by expanding the scope of the Plan’s inﬂuence. Some of the 
ways in which the Plan has been incorporated or referenced into other planning mechanisms are summarized 
below:

The Plan will continue to function as a standalone document subject to its own review and revision schedule. 
The Plan will also serve as a reference for other mitigation and land planning needs of the participating 
jurisdictions. Whenever possible, the jurisdictions will endeavor to incorporate the risk assessment results and 
mitigation measures identiﬁed in the Plan, into existing and future planning mechanisms. This incorporation 
may include but not limited to natural resources and safety elements of general and comprehensive plans, 
adding or revising building codes and zoning and subdivision ordinances. 
There are several challenges to incorporating the Plan and its elements into other planning efforts. First it is not 
always possible due to the time periods represented in other plans or lack of planning efforts due to the small 
size of the communities in this Plan. Some of the planning efforts may not require regular updating due to the 
slow growth experienced in the Planning Area. However, the Planning Team is committed to publicizing the Plan 
when approved to ensure when community plans and programs are reviewed and/or updated it is used as a 
resource.

RESOLUTION ____-25 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF NAVAJO COUNTY, 
ARIZONA, AUTHORIZING THE ADOPTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY HAZARD 
MITIGATION PLAN 2024 UPDATE 
 
 
WHEREAS,  all jurisdictions within Navajo County have exposure to natural hazards that 
increase the risk to life, property, environment, the County and local economy; and 
 
WHEREAS, all jurisdictions within Navajo County have exposure to natural hazards that increase 
the risk to life, property, environment, the County and local economy; and 
 
WHEREAS, Navajo County has prepared a multi-hazard mitigation plan, hereby known as Navajo 
County Multi-Jurisdiction Hazard Mitigation Plan 2024 in accordance with federal laws, including 
the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, as amended; the National 
Flood Insurance Act of 1968, as amended; and the National Dam Safety Program Act, as amended; 
and 
 
WHEREAS, Navajo County Multi-Jurisdiction Hazard Mitigation Plan 2024 identifies mitigation 
goals and actions to reduce or eliminate long-term risk to people and property in Navajo County 
from the impacts of future hazards and disasters; and 
 
WHEREAS, a coalition of Navajo County municipalities with like planning objectives has been 
formed to pool resources. The coalition has completed a planning process that engages the public, 
assesses the risk and vulnerability to the impacts of natural hazards, develops a mitigation strategy 
consistent with a set of uniform goals and objectives, and creates a plan for implementing, 
evaluating and revising this strategy; and 
 
WHEREAS, adoption by the Navajo County demonstrates its commitment to hazard mitigation 
and achieving the goals outlined in the Navajo County Multi-Jurisdiction Hazard Mitigation Plan 
2024. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE  IT RESOLVED BY THE NAVAJO  COUNTY BOARD OF 
SUPERVISORS AS FOLLOWS:  
 
Section 1. In accordance with (local rule for adopting resolutions), the Navajo County 
Board of Supervisors adopts the Navajo County Multi-Jurisdiction Hazard Mitigation 
Plan 2024. While content related to Navajo County may require revisions to meet the

<!-- page 402 -->
plan approval requirements, changes occurring after adoption will not require Navajo 
County  to re-adopt any further iterations of the plan. Subsequent plan updates following 
the approval period for this plan will require separate adoption resolutions. 
 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors on this 
___ day of ___________, 2025.  
 
 NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
 
 
 By ________________________________________ 
                                                                            Jason Whiting,  Chairman of the Board

Board of Supervisors Regular 4. a.        
Meeting Date: 06/24/2025  
Title: Funds for extension of 7th South Street, Snowflake 
Submitted For: William Flake, Assistant County Engineer 
Submitted By: Donald Perkins, Flood Control Manager
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Will Flake
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of an Intergovernmental Agreement with the Town of Snowflake requesting financial
assistance for the extension of the 7th South Street Project in the amount of $120,000.
Background:
The Town of Snowflake plans to improve East 7th South Street to ease traffic on 9th South Street.  Better
entry and exit are needed for this area.
The Town of Snowflake has engaged the services of a local engineering firm to design a project to install
necessary drainage pipes and extend East 7th South Street to the 2nd Street East alignment and extend
2nd Street East southward to the existing 2nd Street East extension.
The Town requests that Navajo County reimburse them for eligible costs for this project, up to a
maximum of $120,000.  
Eligible costs are actual expenses associated with the cost of project construction.
Copies of paid invoices for the project shall be submitted to Navajo County for reimbursement.
 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval.

Motion before the Board:

Barn located at 7863 White Mountain Lake Road, Show Low, AZ.
Background:
We received a 007 Beer and Wine Bar liquor license application from Jeffrey Craig Miller
(Agent) for The 4S Barn. The Sheriff's Office, Health Department and Planning and Development have
all responded that the application meets the requirements of their department.  The Treasurer's Office has
advised that the second half of taxes are unpaid and past due.  The 21-day posting requirement has been
completed.  
 
Recommendation:

Consideration of a request by Steve Kohner for a Master Development Plan Amendment from
an approved, approximately 80-unit, single family residential subdivision to be amended to
allow for 49 single family lots, 74 townhome units, and changes to the roadways as well as open
spaces in the Starlight Ridge Estates Special Development within the Wagon Wheel area.
APN#: 212-05-007N, 212-05-007P, 212-05-007Q, 212-05-007R, 212-05-007S, T09N, R22E,
S08 of the GSRM. Owner: TST Holdings. Agent: Steve Kohner.
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:
The land in the vicinity of this project is zoned Special Development or A-General. The
Starlight Ridge Estates #2 subdivision lies directly north of this project. Starlight Ridge Estates
Townhouses #2 lies directly to the east of this project, as does Starlight Ridge Estates #1, and
vacant, A-General land sits to the southeast of this project. The Fort Apache Indian
Reservation borders this project to the west, as well as the south.
BACKGROUND/HISTORY:
There is an existing, approved Master Development Plan for this project. This MDP was
amended in 2006, and a tentative plat was approved by the Planning and Zoning Commission
in same year. This approval allowed for 53 acres of the subject parcels to be developed out to a
maximum of 80 single-family home units.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
This project is designed to contain the following components, split into two phases of
development:
 Phase 1 will consist of 49 single-family lots and will be located on the northern 31.90
acres of this project.
 Phase 2 will consist of 74 townhome units and will be located on the remaining southern
21.10 acres of this project.
 Connection to the City of Show Low water system.
 Connection to the Pinetop Sanitary Sewer District.
 Fire hydrants installed at 400ft intervals.
 Paved onsite and access roads.

1. The purpose of the Special Development zone is to provide for the development of
subdivisions and other land use projects containing various dwelling types, necessary
commercial centers, off street parking areas, open space areas for recreation, and to preserve
a rural atmosphere.

Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 1  
1.0 INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY 
1.1 Introduction 
Lee Engineering has prepared this report to present the results of a traffic analysis for Starlight 
Ridge Estates, a proposed residential development of 74 townhomes and 49 single -family homes 
near SR 260, about 0.85 miles west of the intersection of SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Lane in 
Lakeside, Arizona. The objective of this analysis is to prepare a traffic impact analysis (TIA)  
sufficient to satisfy the req uirements of the Arizona Department of Transportation of 
Transportation (ADOT) as outlined in its Traffic Guidelines and Processes (TGP) Section 240. 
 
Pre-TIA documentation was submitted to ADOT for review on February 13, 2023, and approval 
with comments was received on June 23, 2023. It is noted that the developer initially intended for 
the site to consist of 196 lots to support tiny homes. However, the land use was later modified to 
include the above -identified mix of residential units . This report was prepared following the 
assumptions and methodolo gies documented in the Pre -TIA for a Category I analysis (small 
development generating over 100 peak-hour trips but fewer than 500). Comments received on the 
pre-TIA document have been addressed as part of this report. 
 
The original report for this project was prepared in February 2024.  However, it was unclear if the 
report was submitted for agency review as no formal comments were received.  As part of client 
phone conversations that have occurred between the property owner and/or other local agencies , 
it is understood two elements from the original report have changed: 
1. Access between the site and Wagon Wheel Road is not currently possible as an agreement 
to obtain an easement across Bureau of Indian Affairs property has not been reached.  On-
going efforts to obtain the agreement continues. 
2. Due to delays in obtaining the agreement, the construction schedule/opening year for Phase 
1 of the project is now anticipated for Fall 2025. 
 
An undated report dated December 2024 was prepared.  This  report continued to assume a Phase 
1 opening for 2024 for consistency; however, site recommendations continue to be based on full 
build-out/occupancy of the site in 2027, which has not been modified from the original report.  
Section 6.4 was added to the report to address the potential loss of Wagon Wheel Road use.   
 
This current version of the report incorporates comments received from Navajo County (dated 
February 11, 2025) pertaining to  the December 2024 report. County comments and Lee 
Engineering responses are provided in Appendix A.  Modifications to the December 2024 report 
are reflected in the Executive Summary, Sections 6.4 and 6.5, and in the Recommendations of this 
report. The remainder of the report has not been modified. 
 
1.2 Executive Summary 
1.2.1 Site Location and Study Area 
The subject approximately 52.96-acre property is located near SR 260, about 0.85 miles west of 
the intersection of SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Lane, having Navajo County Assessor Parcel

<!-- page 569 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 2  
Numbers 212-05-007N, 212 -05-007P, 212-05-007Q, 212-05-07R, and 212 -05-007S, located in 
Lakeside, Arizona. 
 
The study area includes the following locations: 
• SR 260 and Webb Drive. 
• SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Lane. 
• SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Road. 
1.2.2 Development Description 
The site is planned for development in two phases encompassing about 52.96 acres, 74 townhomes, 
and 49 single-family detached lots (31 half-acre lots and 18 10,000 sq ft lots), planned for opening 
in late 2024. 
 
Three access points  are proposed for the site  to the existing local roadway network that will 
ultimately intersect SR 260 via Webb Drive, Wagon Wheel Lane,  and Wagon Wheel Road. The 
three intersections currently and are to remain full-movement intersections.   
1.2.3 Principal Findings 
Based on the analysis conducted in this study, the following conclusions are presented: 
• Starlight Ridge Estates is planned for a total of 123 dwelling units that is to be constructed 
in two phases having an estimated opening year scheduled for late 2024.  
• Peak-period turning movement counts were collected in August 2023. Peak hour  
conditions were found to occur beginning at 7:30 a.m., 11:00 a.m., and 3:30 p.m.  
• The study area intersections experienced an average of 1.0 collision per year during a 5 -
year analysis period, an indication of very good safety performance. 
• The count data was determined to be collected during peak-season conditions, an estimated 
24% above calculated ADT conditions.  No seasonal adjustment factors were applied, 
acting as a conservative (high) estimate of volume conditions to be evaluated. 
• Under existing 2023 conditions, all movements in the study area operate at acceptable 
LOS C or better  conditions during the morning, midday, and afternoon peak periods, 
except the westbound approach  at the Wagon Wheel Lane intersection (LOS E/F) . 
However, the v/c ratios of this non -site approach indicate it is operating well below 
capacity. 
• To project current volume to analysis year conditions, traffic volumes were increased by 
3% per year, slightly above the ADOT straight-line volume estimate of 2.3% per year. 
• Under 2024 and 2027 Background conditions, all movements at the SR 260/Webb Drive 
and Wagon Wheel Road intersections are expected to operate at acceptable LOS D or better 
conditions during each peak period.  At the Wagon Wheel Lane intersection, both 
eastbound and westbound approaches are expected to operate at LOS E/F during peak time 
periods, but have a low v/c ratio (0.50 or less eastbound, 0.24 or less westbound) indicating 
elevated delays but with available movement capacity.  
• Based on ITE Trip Generation estimates, the development is to generate a total of 1,037 
daily trip ends, 72 morning peak -hour, 54 midday, and 92 afternoon peak-hour trips.  No 
reduction for internal capture, alternative travel modes, or pass-by trips have been applied 
or are applicable.

<!-- page 570 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 3  
• Site traffic was assumed to distribute 50% to and from the north, and 50% to and from the 
south along SR 260. 
• Under 2027 Total conditions, 3 -years after site opening and an assumption the site is 
completely built-out and fully occupied, all movements at the Webb Drive and Wagon 
Wheel Road intersections continue to operate in an acceptable manner at LOS D or better.  
At Wagon Wheel Lane, the eastbound and westbound approaches show slightly increased 
delays and v/c ratios as compared to background conditions, however, the delays, v/c ratios, 
and 95th percentile queue remain relatively similar with the site-added traffic.  
• To mitigate/improve the poor intersection performance at Wagon Wheel Lane, a simple 
reallocation of some exiting site traffic from Wagon Wheel Lane to Webb Drive was 
accomplished, minimizing the impact of the outbound left -turn movements turning onto 
northbound SR 260.  Results indicate the Webb Drive intersection can operate at LOS D 
while the SR/260/Wagon Wheel Lane intersection can operate at LOS D during the AM 
peak hour and LOS E during the midday and PM peak with a v/c ratio of 0.50 or less, 
operating slightly better than in the 2027 Background conditions.  
• It is likely that other site and non -site traffic at the eastbound approach to Wagon Wheel  
Lane could also relocate if delays become predictable and excessive, noting familiarity 
with the local street network.  Similarly, vehicles at the westbound Wagon Wheel Lane 
approach have two other SR 260 access points they could redistribute to (Wild Game Trail 
and Dear Run Road) if so desired to minimize delay.  
• MUTCD signal W arrants 1 and 2 were reviewed at the SR 260/ Wagon Wheel Lane 
intersection.  Results indicate both warrants are met at the 70% threshold values under the 
2027 Background and 2027 Total volume scenarios.  However, the installation of a traffic 
signal is not mandatory nor believed to be appropriate, due to the following reasons:   
o Analysis was conducted using peak-season traffic volumes. 
o The volumes assume full site build-out and occupancy by 2027.  This may not occur 
noting the development is planned for multiple phases. 
o Other non-site drivers could relocate to a different SR 260 approach if desired. 
o Wagon Wheel Lane is only 0.41 miles from the signalized Scott Ranch Road 
intersection, a distance within the half-mile spacing preferred by ADOT. 
o It is possible that more or larger gaps are created in the SR 260 traffic stream by 
the existing Scott Ranch Road intersection, improving the study area intersection 
performance as presented herein. 
o Many of the estimated side -street hourly volumes barely met the 70% MUTCD 
threshold values without assuming any right -turn reductions.  To improve 
operations, the Wagon Wheel Lane eastbound approach could be widened to 
include a left and a shared through -right lane. permitting simultaneous right - and 
left-turn movements.  This would be a preferred option in case site access to Wagon 
Wheel Road is not available in the near future. 
• Supplemental analysis indicates the northwest corner of the SR 260/Wagon Wheel Lane 
intersection could be modified without having to obtain additional right-of-way. A 
preliminary analysis indicates the Wagon Wheel Lane approach could be widened to 
permit a pavement width of 33 feet to allow two 10 -foot approach lanes and a 13 -foot 
receiving lane. Utility relocation would be required. 
• Supplemental analysis suggests that the Wagon Wheel Lane widening should be installed 
prior to the occupancy permit for the 24th dwelling unit being provided.

<!-- page 571 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 4  
 
Based on the analysis conducted in this study, the following recommendations are presented: 
 
 Site Developer 
• To minimize site-related impacts, continue to pursue direct access from the site to Rim 
Road/Wagon Wheel Road.  If and when an agreement has been reached, the roadway 
segment between the site and Wagon Wheel Road should be paved. 
• Ensure adequate intersection sight visibility is provided from the site access points onto 
Wagon Wheel Lane.  At a minimum, 280 feet of unobstructed sight visibility is to be 
provided. 
• If site access via Wagon Wheel Road is not possible, widen the eastbound Wagon 
Wheel Lane approach to SR 260.  The eastbound approach should accommodate a left-
turn lane and a shared through/right -turn lane, the left -turn lane having a 75-foot 
storage length.  Utility relocation will be required.  A preliminary schematic of the 
improvement is contained in this report.  A more detailed investigation and design 
could be advanced with agency agreement of concept  outside of this report .  Any 
improvement requires approval and coordination with Navajo County and ADOT.  
 
ADOT and Navajo County 
• Analysis indicates no SR 260 roadway improvements are required to accommodate the 
subject site traffic.  
• A traffic signal is warranted at the SR 260 intersection with Wagon Wheel Lane 
(meeting Warrants 1B and 2 under 2027 Background and Total traffic conditions),  
however, a signal at this intersection would be within the ADOT preferred half -mile 
spacing of the traffic signal at Scott Ranch Road and is not recommended. 
• If site access is available via Wagon Wheel Road, elevated side-street peak-hour delays 
(LOS E, v/c < 0.50, 95% queue <75 feet ) may be acceptable as drivers have multiple 
access options to SR 260.  
• If site access is not avai lable via Wagon Wheel Road, the eastbound Wagon Wheel 
Lane should be widened to accommodate 2 approach lanes while maintaining minor-
street stop control.   
• Any improvement at the Wagon Wheel Lane approach to SR 260 should be in  place 
before the residential development is issued its 25th occupancy permit. 
 
2.0 PROPOSED DEVELOPMENT 
2.1 Site Location and Study Area 
The planned residential development is to be situated on a 52.96-acre property, about 0.85 miles 
west of SR 260 (White Mountain Boulevard).  The site includes  Navajo County APNs 212 -05-
007N, 212-05-007P, 212-05-007Q, 212-05-007R, and 212-05-007S located in Lakeside, Arizona. 
A vicinity map is provided in Figure 1.

<!-- page 572 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 5  
Figure 1: Vicinity Map 
 
 
ADOT TGP 240 guidance requires the study area of Category I TIAs to include adjacent signalized 
intersections and major unsignalized intersections within ½ mile of the development.  Due to the 
location of the site, all site-related traffic will utilize the low-volume local street network to access 
SR 260, hence, all study area intersections to be analyzed are located on SR 260.   
2.2 Land Use and Intensity 
The site is planned to consist of 49 single-family homes and 74 townhomes equal to 123 total lots.  
The Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE) land use codes (LUC) that best describe the 
proposed development include: 
• LUC #210 – Single Family Detached Housing and 
• LUC #215 – Single-Family Attached Housing  
 
The overall proposed density planned for the site is 2.3 dwelling units per acre (123 DU / 53 Ac).

<!-- page 573 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 6  
2.3 Site Plan & Access Geometrics 
A conceptual site layout plan for the proposed development is provided in  Figure 2. The site has 
the following general characteristics: 
• A total of 74 townhomes and 49 single -family homes are planned for development .  The 
townhomes are to be constructed in clusters of 3 to 6 units confined to the southern portion 
of the property while the single-family homes are proposed to be built on individual lot 
sizes between 0.2 and 0.82 acres planned for the northern section of the property.  
• Access to the site is planned from 3  locations intersecting the local roadway network, 
ultimately providing access to and from SR 260 .  Site-generated trips will be able to SR 
260 via Webb Drive, Wagon Wheel Lane, and Wagon Wheel Road.  
 
2.4 Development Phasing and Timing 
The subject development is expected to be developed in two phases, with the first phase anticipated 
for opening in late 2024.  For the purposes of this analysis and following ADOT guidance, build-
out and full occupancy of the site has been accelerated to the 2024 opening year. 
 
3.0 STUDY AREA CONDITIONS 
3.1 Study Area 
Per an approved ADOT Traffic Impact Analysis Pre -Submittal (Appendix B), ADOT requested 
the study area to include the following intersections: 
 
• SR 260 and Webb Drive. 
• SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Lane. 
• SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Road. 
3.2 Existing Land Use and Anticipated Future Development 
The site property is currently undeveloped and in its natural state.  Adjacent to the site, the 
following land uses are noted: 
• South and West of site: Undeveloped land, identified as Fort Apache Indian Reservation. 
• North of site: undeveloped. 
• East of site: Residential parcels. 
 
At this time, no future development that will generate a significant amount of vehicular traffic is 
proposed within the study area.  Additionally, no planned or programmed improvements have been 
identified that will significantly change operational conditi ons within the study area prior to the 
opening of the site.

3.3 Site Accessibility 
Access to the site is proposed from 2 paved access points on Wagon Wheel Lane, ultimately 
providing access to SR 260 at Webb Drive (via Starlight Ridge Road) and Wagon Wheel Lane. A 
3rd access point, indicated as a gravel drive beyond the property line to Rim Road, is located at the 
south end of the site.  Rim Road provides connection to Wagon Wheel Road which also intersects 
SR 260 to the east.  
 
Due to the site’s location all site -related traffic is expected to use SR 260.  Travel on SR 260 to 
the north provides access to the downtown Show Low area while southward travel directs vehicles 
to the Pinetop-Lakeside area.  
 
 
4.0 ANALYSIS OF EXISTING CONDITIONS 
4.1 Physical Characteristics 
Roadway Characteristics 
Roadways in the study area have the following characteristics: 
 
State Route 260 is a four-lane Principal Highway with continuous two-way left-turn lane (TWLTL) 
striping within the study area. This roadway provides access to many side streets and development 
driveways without right-turn deceleration lanes at many of its low-volume side street intersections. 
The roadway is posted with a 45-mph speed limit. Aerial imagery shows curb, gutter, and sidewalk 
are present on the east and west sides of SR 260 in the immediate vicinity of the site. Roadway 
lighting and bike lanes do not exist in the vicinity of the subject site. 
 
Webb Drive, Wagon Wheel Lane, and Wagon Wheel Road are local two-lane undivided east-west 
roadways providing access to residential parcels and small retail and commercial properties that 
line SR 260. No bike lanes, sidewalks, or roadway lighting exist  along the three local roadways . 
The posted speed limit on each roadway is 25 mph. 
 
Intersections and Traffic Control Devices 
• The intersection of SR 260 and Webb Drive (Intersection 1) is a 3-leg minor-street stop-
controlled intersection. The intersection has two northbound through lanes, two 
southbound through lanes, and a shared eastbound right and left -turn lane. Crosswalk 
ramps are present on the northwest and southwest corners of the intersection for crossing 
Webb Drive.  The intersection operates without turn restriction and is located less than ¼ 
mile south from the signalized intersection of SR 260 and Scott Ranch Road. 
• The intersection of SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Lane is a 4-leg minor-street stop-controlled 
intersection. The intersection has two northbound through lanes, two southbound through 
lanes, a shared eastbound right and left -turn lane, and a shared westbound right and left -
turn lane. Crosswalk ramps are present on all four corners . This intersection is located 
about 0.25 miles south of Webb Drive.  
• The intersection of SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Road is a 3-leg minor-street stop-controlled 
intersection. The intersection has two northbound through lanes, two southbound through 
lanes, and a shared eastbound right and left-turn lane.  The eastbound approach is slightly

<!-- page 576 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 9  
angled permitting separate eastbound right and left -turn movements (1 vehicle storage) . 
The intersection is located about 0.5 miles south of Wagon Wheel Lane.

Over the two-year period between 2020 and 2022, traffic on SR 260 increased at an annual rate of 
approximately 2.4%. Additionally, traffic is expected to continue to increase at an annual rate of 
2.3% between 2022 and 2042 based on ADOT projections. Hence an annual growth rate of 3.0% 
was assumed for future traffic growth calculations to act as a conservative (high) estimate of traffic 
volumes conditions. 
 
2023 Traffic Volumes 
Turning movements at the intersection s of SR 260 with Webb Drive, Wagon Wheel Lane, and 
Wagon Wheel Road were collected by Field Data Services  on Wednesday, August 2, 2023 . 
Turning movement counts were collected for 24 hours at each location.  The raw data counts are 
provided in Appendix C. 
 
Seasonal Traffic Volume Adjustment Considerations 
Review of historical 24-hour traffic volumes on SR 260 indicated average daily traffic (ADT) of 
24,795 vehicles in 2022. Using the assumed growth rate of 3.0%, ADT in 2023 was estimated to 
be 25,539 vehicles per day (VPD). The count data collected by Field Data Services in August 2023 
indicated a 24-hour volume of 31,768 vehicles, about 24% higher than the value estimated using 
the historical traffic volumes.  Therefore, it was assumed that the collected August volumes 
represent peak-season conditions.  For study purposes, the volumes were not downward adjusted 
to represent average conditions.  The higher volumes will act as a conservative (high) estimate of 
traffic conditions and the resulting intersection performance measures will show higher delays 
than that of the typical day. 
 
Existing Study Area Considerations 
The results of data collection indicate the study area’s morning, mid-day, and afternoon peak hours 
began at 7:30 a.m., 11:00 a.m., and 3:30 p.m., respectively. The 2023 existing peak-hour volumes, 
lane configurations at the study intersections, and current traffic control are presented in Figure 3.

4.3 Existing Level of Service 
The study-area intersections were analyzed based on the methodologies in the Highway Capacity 
Manual 6th Edition (HCM6, 2017) and evaluated using Synchro software (version 11). To provide 
an indication of intersection performance, signalized and unsignalized intersections are typically 
reported in terms of Levels of Service (LOS). Stop-controlled intersection analysis is based on the 
minor street approach or critical movement, whichever is applicable. The capacity criteria for 
signalized and unsignalized intersection analysis are presented in Table 2. 
Table 2: Level of Service Criteria for Signalized/Unsignalized Intersections 
Level of Service 
(LOS) 
Average Control Delay (seconds/vehicle) 
Signalized Unsignalized 
A ≤10.0 ≤10.0 
B >10.0 and ≤20.0 >10.0 and ≤15.0 
C >20.0 and ≤35.0 >15.0 and ≤25.0 
D >35.0 and ≤55.0 >25.0 and ≤35.0 
E >55.0 and ≤80.0 >35.0 and ≤50.0 
F >80.0 >50.0 
Source: Highway Capacity Manual, HCM 6th Edition, Transportation 
Research Board, 2017. 
 
Additional performance measures such as volume to capacity (v/c) ratios and queue lengths also 
provide an indication of operation.  The HCM6 offers the following in Chapter 20:  
“For a typical major street with two lanes in each direction and an average traffic volume in the 
range of 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles/day (roughly equivalent to a peak hour flow rate of 1,500 to 
2,000 vehicles/hour), the delay equation will predict greater than 50s of delay (LOS F) for many 
urban two-way-stop-controlled (TWSC) intersections that allow minor-street left-turn movements.  
LOS F will be predicted regardless of the volume of minor-street left-turning traffic.  Even with a 
LOS F estimate, most low-volume minor-street approaches would not meet any of the volume or 
delay warrants for signalization noted in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices. As a 
result, analysts who use the HCM LOS thresholds as the sole measure to determine the design 
accuracy of TWSC intersections should do so with caution.  In evaluating the overall performance 
of TWSC intersections, it is important to consider measures of effectiveness such as volume -to-
capacity ratios for individual movements, average queue lengths, and 95th percentile queue lengths 
in addition to considering delay.  By focusing on a single measure of effectiveness for the worst 
movement only, such as delay for the minor -street left-turn, users may make less effective traffic 
control decisions.” 
 
For the purposes of this study, TWSC approaches operating at LOS E or F with v/c ratios under 
0.80 will be considered as operating at an acceptable level when the side street traffic volumes do 
not warrant a traffic signal.

<!-- page 579 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 12  
The study area intersections were  evaluated using Synchro software to estimate peak -hour 
performance characteristics.  Peak-hour factors for each movement utilized the ADOT volume 
criteria based on volume per lane group. The results of the analyses are presented in Table 3. All 
capacity output sheets are provided in Appendix D. 
 
Table 3: Intersection Level of Service Summary, 2023 Existing 
 
 
The results under the existing traffic volumes analyzed indicate the following: 
• All movements during the morning peak hour operate at acceptable LOS D or better  
conditions with vehicle queues of less than 2 vehicle lengths at all locations. 
• All movements during the midday and PM peak operate at LOS D or better conditions, 
except for the westbound approach at the Wagon Wheel Lane intersection which operates 
at LOS E/F with v/c ratios of 0.08 and 0.04, respectively.  In this scenario, the westbound 
approach is considered operating acceptably due to the very low v/c values. 
4.4 Safety 
A crash analysis of the latest 5-year period with available crash data (2018 through 2022) was 
conducted for the study area intersections using the ADOT Safety Data Mart database. Crashes are 
summarized in Table 4, leading to the following observations: 
• Five crashes were identified within 300 feet of the intersection of SR 260 and Webb Drive, 
and at the intersection of SR  260 and Wagon Wheel Lane, an average of one crash per 
year at each location. 
• Three crashes were identified within 300 feet of the intersection of SR  260 and Wagon 
Wheel Road, an average of only 0.6 crashes per year. 
• No fatal or severe crashes were reported in the study area.  The majority of crashes 
involved property damage only, while only one crash indicated a minor injury and one a 
possible injury. 
• The manner of collision indicated three left turn crashes, 3 single vehicle crashes, 3 side -
swipe same direction crashes, two rear -end crashes, one head -on crash, and one other 
crash.

5.0 PROJECTED TRAFFIC 
5.1 Site Traffic Forecasts 
Trip Generation 
The ITE Trip Generation Manual (11th Edition) was used to estimate the number of vehicle trip 
ends the subject site is expected to generate.  The land use  codes (LUC) that best describe the 
proposed development  are ITE LUC # 210, Single -Family Detached Housing and LUC #215, 
Single-Family Attached Housing. 
 
Trips were calculated based on the number of dwelling units proposed for each land use type (74 
townhomes and 49 single-family homes). 
 
ITE Time of Day Distribution for Vehicle Trips in the Trip Generation Manual (10th Edition) was 
used to estimate the midday peak hour trips (11 a.m. – 12 p.m.). This spreadsheet provides hourly 
distribution of entering and exiting vehicle trips by land use across a 24-hour period. 
 
Mode Split 
Due to the nature of residential developments, all trips are assumed to be new passenger vehicle 
trips that will be added to the adjacent roadway network. Trip reductions due to transit, walk, bike, 
and alternative travel modes were not considered or applicable. 
 
Pass-by Traffic 
No pass-by traffic has been assumed for the subject development.

5.2 Non-Site Traffic Forecasting 
Since the subject development is considered a Category I in ADOT’s TIA guidelines, analysis of 
the opening year (2024) and 3 -year horizon after opening (2027) was conducted. Background 
traffic can be estimated from the combination of two components: traffic generated from newly 
constructed developments near the site plus ambient growth of the community.  
 
No known nearby developments are expected to be constructed by 2027 to contribute a significant 
amount of traffic to the study area, therefore all additional traffic in the study area will be from the 
general growth of the community.  
 
To determine ambient traffic growth of the study area, background traffic was estimated to grow 
at the historical rate of 3.0% per year, based on ADOT projections.  
 
To estimate 2024 Background conditions (without site traffic), the 2023 traffic volumes in Figure 
3 were increased by 3. 0% to account for one year of traffic growth.  Similarly, to estimate 2027 
horizon year background conditions, the same Figure 3 volumes were increased by 12.6%, or 3.0% 
growth for 4 years. Figure 6 and Figure 7 show the background traffic volumes for each analysis 
year, respectively. 
5.3 Total Traffic Conditions 
To estimate the total traffic volumes for the 2024 opening year of the proposed development, the 
site-related volumes in Figure 5 were added to the volumes in Figure 6. Figure 8 presents the total 
traffic volume conditions estimated for 2024  assuming full site build -out and occupancy  of the 
entire Starlight Ridge Estates. 
 
Similarly, Figure 9 displays the 2027 total volume conditions, estimated by adding together the 
volumes presented in Figure 5 and Figure 7.

Mitigation 1, Site Redistribution - 2027 Total Traffic (Build) Conditions 
Although the SR 260/Wagon Wheel Lane intersection shows elevated delays, the other study 
intersections indicate additional capacity is available to improve overall operations.  Noting the 
eastbound approaches at Webb Drive and Wagon Wheel Road operate with less delay than Wagon 
Wheel Lane, repeat drivers will pursue a travel path with the lowest delay possible, approaching 
delay equilibrium between intersections.  Because the site -generated drivers (and other non -site 
residential motorists) will be familiar  with the adjacent local roadway network, they can easily 
choose an optional travel route different than the distribution percentage and volume condition 
indicated in Figures 4 and 5.  A possible change in site-generated volume as a result of site-traffic 
redistribution at the study intersections is presented in Figure 10.  The results of the intersection 
analysis under this scenario are presented in Table 10.

The results show both Webb Drive and Wagon Wheel Road can continue to operate at LOS D or 
better for each peak period while the eastbound Wagon Wheel Lane approach will operate better 
than in the 2027 Background traffic condition s with lower delay and v/c ratio in the midday and 
PM peak hours , although still operating at LOS E .  It is likely that other non-site traffic at the 
eastbound approach could also relocate if delays become predictable and excessive , if so desired 
noting familiarity with the local network.  Similarly, vehicles at the westbound approach have two 
other SR 260 access points they could redistribute to (Wild Game Trail and Dear Run Road) if so

6.3 Traffic Safety 
Intersection Sight Distance 
AASHTO’s A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets  recommends the following 
minimum intersection sight distance for left- and right-turn movements from a stopped condition 
for departing drivers stopped 15 feet from the edge of the travelled way. It recommends adding 
0.5 seconds for each additional lane, more than one lane, to be crossed, including turn lanes. 
Median width is converted to an equivalent number of lanes and 0.5 seconds is added for each 12 
feet of lane width. 
 
Access to the site is proposed from multiple access points on Wagon Wheel Lane. In the case  of 
vehicles waiting on the stop-controlled minor street to turn left or cross the major roadway (Wagon 
Wheel Lane), sufficient sight distance is needed to accommodate the maneuver. 
 
Table 11 shows the time gap for different types of design vehicles turning left or crossing a 2-lane 
roadway from the minor street. 
Table 11: Time Gap, Left Turns from Minor Street 
 
 
The time gap is determined to be 7.5 seconds for a passenger car, and the posted speed on Wagon 
Wheel Lane is identified to be 25 mph. 
 
The intersection sight distance is calculated as: 
 
𝐼𝑆𝐷 = 1.47 ∗  𝑉𝑚𝑎𝑗𝑜𝑟 ∗ 𝑡𝑔 
𝐼𝑆𝐷 = 1.47 ∗  25 𝑚𝑝ℎ ∗ 7.5 𝑠𝑒𝑐 
𝐼𝑆𝐷 = 275.63 𝑓𝑒𝑒𝑡 (280 𝑓𝑒𝑒𝑡) 
 
A minimum intersection sight distance of 280 feet is needed from the site access points at their 
intersection with Wagon Wheel Lane to safely complete the desired maneuver.

<!-- page 595 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 28  
In the case of vehicles waiting on the minor street to turn right,  Table 12 shows the time gap for 
different types of design vehicles turning from the minor street. 
Table 12: Time Gap, Right Turns from Minor Street 
 
 
A time gap of 6.5 seconds is determined for a passenger car. The intersection sight distance is 
calculated as: 
 
𝐼𝑆𝐷 = 1.47 ∗  𝑉𝑚𝑎𝑗𝑜𝑟 ∗ 𝑡𝑔 
𝐼𝑆𝐷 = 1.47 ∗  25 𝑚𝑝ℎ ∗ 6.5 𝑠𝑒𝑐 
𝐼𝑆𝐷 = 238.88 𝑓𝑒𝑒𝑡 (240 𝑓𝑒𝑒𝑡) 
 
Although a site visit was not performed, review of aerial imagery and the site layout plan indicates 
that an unobstructed line of sight can be provided for drivers to safely enter into the Wagon Wheel 
Lane traffic stream. 
 
Turn Lane Design 
No acceleration or deceleration lanes are proposed or warranted for installation as part of this 
project to and from the subject site noting the number of peak -hour site trips projected, the low-
speed conditions on the adjacent local street network, and the road classification. 
 
Traffic Signal Needs 
The minor street stop-controlled intersection of SR 260 and Wagon Wheel Lane was evaluated to 
determine if volumes are met to warrant consideration of installing a traffic signal. The MUTCD 
contains nine traffic signal warrants outlining specific criteria that may make a traffic signal 
justifiable at an intersection. For the purposes of this analysis, only Warrants 1 and 2 were 
reviewed. It is noted that a signal should only  be installed if one or more MUTCD warrants are 
met. However, satisfaction of warran t does not require the installation of a signal. The traffic 
control needs for this intersection were evaluated at the 70% threshold level since the posted speed 
limit on SR 260 is 45 mph (exceeding the 40 mph threshold). 
 
Warrant 1: Eight-Hour Vehicular Volume 
The 8-hour vehicular volume warrant has two parts: Condition A, applicable where a signal 
may be needed due to a high volume of intersecting traffic, and Condition B, where traffic 
is so heavy on the major street that minor street traffic suffers excessive  delay or conflict. 
If the amount of traffic at an intersection exceeds the threshold in either Condition A or 
Condition B, a signal is warranted under Warrant 1.

<!-- page 596 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside

The 70% threshold values for Warrant 1 Condition A are 420 vph on the major street and

Warrant 2: Four-Hour Vehicular Volume 
 
The four-hour warrant is 
intended for application at 
intersections where traffic 
during any four hours of the 
day reaches a level that a 
signal would be beneficial. 
Figure 4C-1 in the MUTCD 
states that “80 vph applies as 
the lower threshold volume 
for a minor-street approach 
with two more lanes and 60 
vph applies as the lower 
threshold volume for a minor 
street approach with one lane.” In this case, 60 vph is used as the minor-street threshold 
since Wagon Wheel Lane is a one-lane approach. Major and minor street volumes that 
intersect on the upper right side of the warranting line for the indicated lane configuration 
meets criteria, while intersecting volumes on the lower left side of the warranting line does 
not meet criteria. In referencing Table 13, Table 14, and Table 15 above for the major street 
volumes, the fourth highest volume exceeds the 1,000 hourly vehicle threshold along the 
mainline, therefore if the higher of the side street volumes exceed 60 vehicles, Warrant 2 
is met.  Based on the volume conditions presented, Warrant 2 is not met for the 2023 
Existing Condition, but met for the 2027 Background and 2027 Total traffic conditions.

herein. 
 
6.4 Supplemental Analysis, No Access to/from Wagon Wheel Road 
A supplemental analysis has been conducted assuming site access to/from Wagon Wheel Road 
will not be possible due to difficulties in obtaining ROW or an easement from the Bureau of Indian 
Affairs (BIA) to directly access this roadway. Therefore, it was assumed all site-related vehicles 
turning to and from Wagon Wheel Road (Int. #3), as indicated in Figure 5, would be re-routed to 
Wagon Wheel Lane (Int. #2).  No other adjustments or re-routing of vehicles to Webb Drive was 
considered for this analysis.   
 
With the re-routing of vehicles, MUTCD signal Warrant 1B and Warrant 2 will continue to be met 
with the site-added trips, but at higher volume conditions for the minor-street eastbound approach 
as indicated in Table 15.   
 
As a possible improvement strategy for the Wagon Wheel Lane approach to SR 260 without having 
to install a traffic signal, widening of the eastbound approach was assumed while maintaining the 
current minor-street stop control.  The eastbound approach was assumed to accommodate a left 
and a shared through/right lane.  The Synchro results for this scenario are presented in Table 17. 
The capacity analysis output sheets for this scenario are provided in Appendix F. 
 
The results indicate the Wagon Wheel Lane left-turn movement would operate at LOS E/F during 
the peak periods, however, the v/c ratios would be no higher than 0.51 with 95th percentile queues 
of less than 3 vehicles.  This is an indication some turn capacity remains for this movement and 
vehicle queues are not excessive.  The more delayed single-lane westbound approach at this 
intersection shows LOS F operation for each time period.  Similarly, the v/c ratio for each period 
is no higher than 0.27.  As indicated previously, some of the site’s northbound destined drivers 
would likely migrate to Webb Lane where additional capacity is available if outbound delays were 
excessive and repeatable, improving the delays identified for Wagon Wheel Lane. Also, 
westbound approach vehicles have access to other local streets and SR 260 if desired.

6.5 Timing of Improvements 
Table 5 estimates the number of peak -hour trip ends the proposed 49 detached and 74 attached 
single-family dwelling units are expected to generate when constructed.  Supplemental analysis of 
the 2027 Background capacity analysis conditions (Table 7), when considering vehicle 
redistribution, indicates 89 more AM, 6 more Midday, and 9 more PM peak-hour left-turn vehicles 
can be accommodated at the Webb Drive and Wagon Wheel Lane eastbound approaches before 
one of the movements operate at LOS E.  This equates to approximately 50% of the ITE trip 
generation values for the higher delayed Midday and PM peak hours for either land use type.  
Therefore, if access via Wagon Wheel Road is not possible, it is suggested that the Wagon Wheel 
Lane improvements be installed prior to issuing the 25th occupancy permit (detached or attached) 
to the Starlight Ridge Estates.   
   
7.0 CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS 
Based on the analysis conducted in this study, the following conclusions are presented: 
• Starlight Ridge Estates is planned for a total of 123 dwelling units that is to be constructed 
in two phases having an estimated opening year scheduled for late 2024.  
• Peak-period turning movement counts were collected in August 2023. Peak hour  
conditions were found to occur beginning at 7:30 a.m., 11:00 a.m., and 3:30 p.m.  
• The study area intersections experienced an average of 1.0 collision per year during a 5 -
year analysis period, an indication of very good safety performance. 
• The count data was determined to be collected during peak-season conditions, an estimated 
24% above calculated ADT conditions.  No seasonal adjustment factors were applied, 
acting as a conservative (high) estimate of volume conditions to be evaluated. 
• Under existing 2023 conditions, all movements in the study area operate at acceptable 
LOS C or better  conditions during the morning, midday, and afternoon peak periods, 
except the westbound approach  at the Wagon Wheel Lane intersection  (LOS E/F) . 
However, the v/c ratios of this non -site approach indicate it is operating well below 
capacity. 
• To project current volume to analysis year conditions, traffic volumes were increased by 
3% per year, slightly above the ADOT straight-line volume estimate of 2.3% per year. 
• Under 2024 and 2027 Background conditions, all movements at the SR 260/Webb Drive 
and Wagon Wheel Road intersections are expected to operate at acceptable LOS D or better 
conditions during each peak period.  At the Wagon Wheel Lane intersection , both 
eastbound and westbound approaches are expected to operate at LOS E/F during peak time 
periods, but have a low v/c ratio (0.50 or less eastbound, 0.24 or less westbound) indicating 
elevated delays but with available movement capacity.

<!-- page 603 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 36  
• Based on ITE Trip Generation estimates, the development is to generate a total of 1,037 
daily trip ends, 72 morning peak -hour, 54 midday, and 92 afternoon peak-hour trips.  No 
reduction for internal capture, alternative travel modes, or pass-by trips have been applied 
or are applicable. 
• Site traffic was assumed to distribute 50% to and from the north, and 50% to and from the 
south along SR 260. 
• Under 2027 Total conditions, 3-years after site opening and an assumption the site is 
completely built-out and fully occupied, all movements at the Webb Drive and Wagon 
Wheel Road intersections continue to operate in an acceptable manner at LOS D or better.  
At Wagon Wheel Lane, the eastbound and westbound approaches show slightly increased 
delays and v/c ratios as compared to background conditions, however, the delays, v/c ratios, 
and 95th percentile queue remain relatively similar with the site-added traffic.  
• To mitigate/improve the poor intersection performance at Wagon Wheel Lane, a simple 
reallocation of some exiting site traffic from Wagon Wheel Lane to Webb Drive was 
accomplished, minimizing the impact of the outbound left-turn movements turning onto 
northbound SR 260.  Results indicate the Webb Drive intersection can operate at LOS D 
while the SR/260/Wagon Wheel Lane intersection can operate at LOS D during the AM 
peak hour and LOS E during the midday and PM p eak with a v/c ratio at 0.50 or less, 
operating slightly better than in the 2027 Background conditions.  
• It is likely that other site and non -site traffic at the eastbound approach to Wagon Wheel  
Lane could also relocate if delays become predictable and excessive, noting familiarity 
with the local  street network.  Similarly, vehicles at the westbound Wagon Wheel Lane 
approach have two other SR 260 access points they could redistribute to (Wild Game Trail 
and Dear Run Road) if so desired to minimize delay.  
• MUTCD signal W arrants 1 and 2 were reviewed at the SR 260/ Wagon Wheel Lane 
intersection.  Results indicate both warrants are met at the 70% threshold values under the 
2027 Background and 2027 Total volume scenarios.  However, the installation of a traffic 
signal is not mandatory nor believed to be appropriate, due to the following reasons:   
o Analysis was conducted using peak-season traffic volumes. 
o The volumes assume full site build-out and occupancy by 2027.  This may not occur 
noting the development is planned for multiple phases. 
o Other non-site drivers could relocate to a different SR 260 approach if desired. 
o Wagon Wheel Lane is only 0.41 miles from the signalized Scott Ranch Road 
intersection, a distance within the half-mile spacing preferred by ADOT. 
o It is possible that more or larger gaps are created in the SR 260 traffic stream by 
the existing Scott Ranch Road intersection, improving the study area intersection 
performance as presented herein. 
o Many of t he estimated side-street hourly volumes barely met the 70% MUTCD 
threshold values without assuming any right -turn reductions.  To improve 
operations, the Wagon Wheel Lane eastbound approach could be widened to 
include a left and a shared through -right lane permitting simultaneous right - and 
left-turn movements.  This would be a preferred option in case site access to Wagon 
Wheel Road is not available in the near future. 
• Supplemental analysis indicates the northwest corner of the SR 260/Wagon Wheel Lane 
intersection could be modified without having to obtain additional right -of-way. A 
preliminary analysis indicates the Wagon Wheel Lane approach could be widened to

<!-- page 604 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III – Lakeside 
Traffic Impact Study 37  
permit a pavement width of 33 feet to allow two 10 -foot approach lanes and a 13 -foot 
receiving lane. Utility relocation would be required. 
• Supplemental analysis suggests if Wagon Wheel Lane is to be improved, improvements 
should be installed prior to the occupancy permit for the 25th dwelling unit being provided.    
  
Based on the analysis conducted in this study, the following recommendations are presented: 
 
 Site Developer 
• To minimize site-related impacts, continue to pursue direct access from the site to Rim 
Road/Wagon Wheel Road.  If and when an agreement has been reached, the roadway 
segment between the site and Wagon Wheel Road should be paved. 
• Ensure adequate intersection sight visibility is provided from the site access points onto 
Wagon Wheel Lane.  At a minimum, 280 feet of unobstructed sight visibility is to be 
provided. 
• If site access via Wagon Wheel Road is not possible, widen the eastbound Wagon 
Wheel Lane approach to SR 260.  The eastbound approach should accommodate a left-
turn lane and a shared through/right -turn lane, the left -turn lane having a 75-foot 
storage length.  Utility relocation will be required.  A preliminary schematic of the 
improvement is contained in this report.  A more detailed investigation and design 
could be advanced with agency agreement of concept  outside of this report .  Any 
improvement requires approval and coordination with Navajo County and ADOT.  
 
ADOT and Navajo County 
• Analysis indicates no SR 260 roadway improvements are required to accommodate the 
subject site traffic.  
• A traffic signal is warranted at the SR 260 intersection with Wagon Wheel Lane 
(meeting Warrants 1B and 2 under 2027 Background and Total traffic conditions),  
however, a signal at this intersection would be within the ADOT preferred half -mile 
spacing of the traffic signal at Scott Ranch Road and is not recommended. 
• If site access is available via Wagon Wheel Road, elevated side-street peak-hour delays 
(LOS E, v/c < 0.50, 95% queue <75 feet ) may be acceptable as drivers have multiple 
access options to SR 260.  
• If site access is not avai lable via Wagon Wheel Road, the eastbound Wagon Wheel 
Lane should be widened to accommodate 2 approach lanes while maintaining minor-
street stop control.   
• Any improvement at the Wagon Wheel Lane approach to SR 260 should be in  place 
before the residential development is issued its 25th occupancy permit.

Mr. Flake, 
Below is Lee Engineering responses to your recently provided TIA comments to the Starlight Ridge TIA 
report (dated December 2024).  The TIA report has been updated to reflect these changes. 
 
Comment #1, Recommendations in Section 7.0 
The report appears to recommend the following for the site developer: 
1. Continue pursuing the connection from Rim Road to Wagon Wheel Road. 
2. Ensure adequate sight visibility at the intersection of Highway 260/Wagon Wheel Lane. 
3. Widen the eastbound Wagon Wheel Lane approach to Highway 260. 
 
Regarding Item 3, the report states: 
"The eastbound approach should accommodate a left-turn lane and a shared through/right-turn lane, one 
of the lanes having a minimum 75-foot storage length. At a minimum, the Wagon Wheel Lane approach 
should be widened to provide a right-turn flared section." 
This description is unclear and seems contradictory. Based on Section 6.4 and other portions of the report, 
there appears to be a specific requirement to provide a left-turn lane and a shared through/right-turn lane 
at this intersection. Including the suggestion to "provide a right-turn flared section" does not align with this 
requirement and should be omitted for consistency. Please revise this section to clarify the intent and ensure 
the recommendations are straightforward. 
Lee Engineering Response: The report text has been updated to be more concise.

<!-- page 607 -->
Page 2 of 3 
 
Comment #2, Feasibility of Lane Widening on Wagon Wheel Lane 
One of the proposed mitigation measures for increased traffic is widening the eastbound approach on 
Wagon Wheel Lane to accommodate a left-turn lane and a shared through/right-turn lane. However, the 
report assumes there is sufficient room for this new lane configuration without verifying its feasibility. 
The photo below suggests there is little to no room for expansion on the south (right) side, and the 
availability of space on the north (left) side is unclear. This needs to be addressed in the report to avoid 
moving forward with assumptions that may later prove unworkable. Please include an evaluation of the 
physical constraints and confirm whether the proposed lane configuration is feasible. 
. 
Lee Engineering Response:  A preliminary analysis by Painted Sky (schematic attached) shows the Wagon 
Wheel Lane west approach could be widened to the north to accommodate a 3-lane cross-section to 
accommodate a 75-foot left-turn lane before transitioning back down to its existing pavement width within 
the existing 55-foot right-of-way (ROW).  Existing utilities would be impacted and would require relocation 
along with sidewalk and curb work.  The developer has indicated preliminary agreement with conducting 
the improvements, pending additional investigation of conditions.  Additional investigation by Painted Sky 
outside of this TIA will commence after receipt of agency comments.  It is suggested that the lane widths 
for the left and shared through/right approach lanes be minimized such that the single receiving lane can 
be maximized to better accommodate turn movements.   
 
Section 6.4 of the report has been updated to reflect the above. 
 
Comment #3, Timing of Improvements 
The report does not specify when the recommended improvements need to occur. Are we to assume that 
the widening of Wagon Wheel Lane should be part of the original subdivision construction unless the Rim 
Road connection can also be completed at that time? 
The recommendation to "continue pursuing" the Rim Road connection creates ambiguity about whether this 
connection—or the Wagon Wheel Lane widening—is required as part of the initial development. Please 
revise the report to clearly state the timing and conditions under which these improvements are expected to 
be completed.

<!-- page 608 -->
Page 3 of 3 
 
Lee Engineering Response:  Table 5 of the report estimates the number of peak-hour trip ends the 
proposed 49 detached and 74 attached single-family dwelling units are expected to generate when 
constructed.  Supplemental analysis of the 2027 Background Capacity conditions (Table 7), when 
considering vehicle redistribution, indicates 89 more AM, 6 more Midday, and 9 more PM peak-hour left-
turn vehicles can be accommodated at the Webb Drive and Wagon Wheel Lane eastbound approaches 
before one of the movements operate at LOS E.  This equates to approximately 50% of the ITE trip 
generation values for the higher delayed Midday and PM peak hours for either land use type.  Therefore, it 
is suggested that the Wagon Wheel Lane improvements be installed prior to issuing the 25th occupancy 
permit (detached or attached) for the Starlight Ridge Estates.

The proposed parcel for development is located near SR 260, about 0.85 miles west of the intersection of SR 
260 and Wagon Wheel Lane in Lakeside, Arizona .  The development is  identified with Assessor Parcel 
Numbers 212-05-007N, 212 -05-007P, 212 -05-007Q, 212 -05-07R, and 212 -05-007S. The site has 
approximately 1400 feet of frontage along Wagon Wheel Lane. 
 
Brief Description of Project (land use, intensity, timeframe/phasing) 
The conceptual site layout plan is attached. The site is planned to consist of 196 lots to support tiny homes 
on approximately 53 acres, resulting in a density of 4 lots per acre . The site is to be constructed in 5 total 
phases, with the first phase anticipated for opening in 2024. 
 
Proposed Access (number, location, restrictions) 
Access to the site is proposed from multiple access points on Wagon Wheel Lane, ultimately providing access 
to SR 260 at Webb Drive (via Starlight Ridge Road) and Wagon Wheel Lane. Both minor-street stop controlled 
intersections currently serv ing a few local businesses and other residential pa rcels.  A 3rd access point, 
indicated as an unpaved drive to Rim Road at the south end of the site, could also provide access to SR 260, 
but would require improvements to Rim Road that are not being considered by the developer at this time. 
 
Preliminary Assumptions 
Trip Generation 
Tiny Homes is not a category within the latest version of the ITE Trip Generation Manual.  As a surrogate, the 
following land uses were considered: 
• ITE Land Use Code 210, Single Family Detached Housing 
• ITE Land Use Code 220, Multifamily Housing (Low-Rise)

<!-- page 611 -->
Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III, Residential Development – TIA Pre-Submittal 
 
 
 Page 2 of 4 
 
The preliminary trip generation estimate for the subject site, assuming both land uses are shown in Table 1. 
Multifamily Residential will be used for analysis based on the following: 
• The average tiny home lot size is estimated at 3,200 square-feet. 
• Each home provides less than 1,000 square feet of living space. 
• Each unit is anticipated to accommodate a single person or small family units, generating trips more 
in-line with multi-family units having limited vehicle ownership and people of driving age. 
Estimates based on this land use indicate that the tiny homes will generate a total of 1,332 daily trip ends, 84 
AM and 105 PM peak-hour trip ends. All trips are assumed to be made via passenger vehicle. 
 
Table 1. Preliminary Trip Generation Estimate 
 
 
Trip Reductions (Internal Capture, Alternative Travel Mode, and Pass-by)  
All trips are assumed to be new passenger vehicle trips. No reduction for internal capture, alternative travel 
modes, or pass-by trips have been applied or are applicable.   
 
Study Horizon Years 
Per the trip generation estimate  and ADOT’s TIA guidelines, the study falls into a Category I analysis ( Small 
Development) generating over 100 peak-hour trips but less than 500. Analysis of the opening year (2024) and 
a 3-year horizon after opening will be conducted.  
  
Trip Distribution 
Vehicles will be distributed and assigned to the adjacent roadway network based on engineering judgment 
and patterns observed in traffic volume data to be collected.  
 
Study Area Intersections 
Considering ADOT’s requirements for a Category I analysis (adjacent signalized intersections and/or major 
unsignalized intersections within 0.5 miles), the following intersection locations will be included within the 
study area and will require data collection:

Starlight Ridge Estates Unit III, Residential Development – TIA Pre-Submittal 
 
 
 Page 3 of 4 
 
 
Study Area Intersections and Turning Movement Count Locations (weekday) 
• SR 260 at Webb Drive 
• SR 260 at Wagon Wheel Lane 
• SR 260 at Wagon Wheel Road 
 
Turning movement count data will be collected at the above intersection locations for a 6-hour period during 
typical weekday conditions (6 to 9AM and 3 to 6PM) to determine existing peak-hour traffic volume data. 
One intersection will be selected to capture vehicle classifications to identify vehicle composition. 
 
Other Considerations – Study Analysis 
Collected count data will be adjusted according to agency direction or engineering judgment to account for 
changes in traffic volume due to seasonal variation (dependent upon data to be collected).  An annual traffic 
growth rate (currently estimated at 3% per year, see below ) will be applied based on previous traffic data 
collected in the vicinity  and used to estimate background traffic volumes for the required analysis years. If 
indicated and information provided, other site-adjacent developments will also be considered. 
 
The location of the count station along SR 260 is about 2 miles south of Wagon Wheel Lane.

Navajo County - For Official Use Only
RESOLUTION ____-25
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS APPROVING
A MASTER DEVELOPMENT PLAN AMENDMENT FOR STARLIGHT RIDGE
ESTATES III SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT
WHEREAS, an application for a Master Development Plan Amendment was duly filed
on January 18th, 2024, by Steve Kohner to allow for 49 single family lots, 74 townhome units, and
changes to the roadways as well as open spaces in the Starlight Ridge Estates Special Development
within the Wagon Wheel area; and
WHEREAS, the application concerns the following real property in Navajo County:
APN # 212-05-007N, 212-05-007P, 212-05-007Q, 212-05-007R, 212-05-007S, Township 09
North, Range 22 East, Section 08 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian; and
WHEREAS, the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on April 17th, 2025; and
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors after considering the testimony
and other evidence presented at the hearing, as well as the recommendations of Staff, found that
the Master Development Plan Amendment is consistent with the public health, safety and general
welfare and should be approved subject to the conditions set forth herein; and
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED  the Board of Supervisors hereby
approves the Master Development Plan Amendment, subject to the following conditions:
1. All Federal, State, and Navajo County permits required for each lot must be obtained and
adhered to.
2. This Master Development Site Plan shall allow for a maximum of 49 single family lots,
and 74 townhome units.
3. A Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA), Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, Sanitary Sewer
Collection System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design Report for the
development, prepared by a Professional Engineer, licensed in the State of Arizona, shall
be submitted to and approved by the County Engineer’s office before the Tentative Plat
and/or Site Plan Review is submitted to the Planning and Zoning Commission.
4. All required offsite improvements identified in the TIA, Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain
Study, Sanitary Sewer Collection System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design

<!-- page 700 -->
Navajo County - For Official Use Only
Report shall be constructed or financially assured before the stage of development is
constructed that requires the improvement.
5. Sufficient off-road drainage easements shall be made available to accommodate major
drainage as required.
6. Drainage structures, including detention or retention ponds, shall be proposed with the
Final Plat and/or Site Plan Review, as required.
7. Access improvements to this site shall be required, at the expense of the developer, which
shall be according to an accepted and approved Final TIA by the Public Works Department.
8. A minimum of 280 feet of unobstructed sight visibility shall be provided at the access
points along Wagon Wheel Road.
9. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations shall be met before approval of
the Tentative Plat and/or Site Plan Review. Variances shall be requested in accordance with
Section 4.12.
10. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations and Requirements, Flood
Control Ordinance, Building Safety Ordinance, and applicable codes shall be adhered to
and approved at the proper Tentative Plat, Final, or Building Permit and construction phase
(to include, without limitation, the Traffic Impact Analysis, Drainage Study, Floodplain
Study, Construction Improvement Plans, and Grading Plans).
11. Approval of the Master Development Site Plan is conditioned upon the submittal for a
request for either a Tentative Plat or for a Site Plan Review to the Planning and Zoning
Commission, along with proof of compliance with the above conditions, within 24 months
of the date of Board of Supervisors Resolution. If this condition is not met, approval shall
be revoked, and the Master Development Site Plan shall become null and void. This
condition shall be conclusively deemed to have been satisfied unless the Board of
Supervisors causes a notice of revocation to be recorded in the Office of the Navajo County
Recorder within 30 days after the expiration of the 24-month period (or any extension
thereof).

RECOMMENDATION
Navajo County Planning and Development Services Staff recommend
approval of the Master Development Plan Amendment for Starlight
Ridge Estates Unit III, subject to 11 conditions:
MDP-A 24-001 11
1. All Federal, State, and County permits required must be obtained and
adhered to.
2. MDP-A shall allow for a maximum of 49 single-family lots, and 74
townhome units.
3. A TIA, Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, Sanitary Sewer Collection
System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design Report shall be
submitted and approved before Tentative Plat is submitted to the Planning
and Zoning Commission.
4. All required offsite improvements identified in the above studies shall be
constructed or financially assured before the stage of development is
constructed that requires the improvement.
5.Sufficient off-road drainage easements shall be made available to
accommodate major drainage as required.
6. Drainage structures, including detention or retention ponds, shall be
proposed with the Final Plat, as required.
7. Access improvements to this site shall be required, at the expense of the
developer, which shall be according to an accepted and approved Final TIA
by the Public Works Department.
8. A minimum of 280 feet of unobstructed sight visibility shall be provided at
the access points along Wagon Wheel Road.
9. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations shall be met
before approval of the Tentative Plat.
10. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations, Flood Control
Ordinance, Building Safety Ordinance, and applicable codes shall be
adhered to and approved at the proper Tentative Plat, Final, or Building
Permit and construction phase.
11. Approval of the Master Development Site Plan is conditioned upon the
submittal for a request for either a Tentative Plat to the Planning and Zoning
Commission, along with proof of compliance with the above conditions,
within 24 months of the date of Board of Supervisors Resolution.
