the permit/agreement application. 
 
z. Use of Permit, Terms and Conditions. 
 
i. Any Renewable Energy Generation facility that is granted an SUP shall be 
developed in accordance with the schedule for development and conditions 
set forth in the SUP. 
 
ii. SUP for a Renewable Energy Generation facility shall be valid for the 
anticipated useful life of the project. 
 
iii. SUP for a Renewable Energy Generation facility shall be granted in the 
name of the applicant and may be transferred or assigned to a new holder 
only with the written approval of the Board of Supervisors, following a 
public hearing. The new holder shall onl y be bound to agree to all existing 
conditions and shall provide adequate assurances to demonstrate that the 
new holder has the financial ability to fulfill the obligations as specified in 
the SUP. 
 
aa.  Permit Suspension and Revocation 
 
i. Any SUP issued pursuant to this section may be suspended or revoked in 
whole or part by the Board of Supervisors for material non-compliance with 
the requirements of this section or the stipulations set forth in the SUP.  
SUP shall be subject to suspension or revocation at a duly noticed public 
hearing only if the SUP holder has failed to cure the material non -
compliance after no less than thirty (30) days’ written notice of such non -
compliance from the Director.

<!-- page 777 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   48 
 
 
ii. If a Renewable Energy Generation facility becomes unsafe or inoperable, 
the SUP is likewise subject to suspension or revocation by the Board of 
Supervisors as follows: 
 
1) An “inoperable Renewable Energy Generation facility” is one that does 
not generate a significant amount of electricity for one-hundred eighty 
(180) consecutive days, unless such non -generation is due to an act of 
nature, declared emergency or other cause beyond the reasonable 
control of the SUP holder or unless the SUP holder demonstrates that 
modernization, rebuilding or repairs are in progress or are planned and 
will be diligently completed. 
 
2) An “unsafe Renewable Energy Generation facility” is one that has been 
found by a state or federal administrative agency or a court of competent 
jurisdiction to have materially violated applicable health or safety laws, 
unless the SUP holder demonstrates th at measures to cure such 
violations are in progress or are planned and will be diligently 
completed. 
 
3) Every unsafe or inoperable Renewable Energy Generation facility is 
hereby declared to be a public nuisance per se which shall be subject to 
abatement by all available legal and equitable remedies. 
 
4) Upon a complaint by the Director that a Renewable Energy Generation 
facility is inoperable or unsafe, the Board of Supervisors shall convene 
a public hearing at the earliest possible date after written notice to the 
SUP holder. Pending a final determination that the facility is inoperable 
or unsafe, the Board may suspend the SUP in whole or part or impose 
such conditions as may be appropriate to protect the public health, 
safety and welfare. Upon a final determination that the facility is 
inoperable or  unsafe, the Board may suspend or revoke the SUP in 
whole or part or impose such conditions as may be appropriate to 
protect the public health, safety and welfare. 
 
iii. No later than thirty (30) days after the revocation or expiration of the SUP, 
the decommissioning plan required by this Section shall be implemented 
and decommissioning shall proceed diligently to completion.

<!-- page 778 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   49 
 
Section 1202 – Wind Energy Generation Facilities 
The following provisions shall be specific for the review of Wind Energy Generation Facilities: 
1. Audible sound limits:  
 
a. Audible noise due to project operations shall not exceed the greater of: (a) 45 dBA 
LAeq,10; or,  
 
b. The measured background, LA90,10 plus 5 dB, as measured at the exterior at any legal 
residence, school, library or hospital in existence at the time of approval of the SUP.  
 
2. If sound levels resulting from a proposed facility exceed the criteria specified above, a 
waiver may be granted after review and recommendation by the Planning and 
Development Services Department, provided that the following has been accomplished:  
 
a.  An irrevocable written consent (or sound waiver easement) has been obtained 
from each affected property owner, stating that the owner is aware of the proposed 
facility and the sound limitations imposed by this section, that consent is granted 
to allow sound levels to exceed the maximum limits specified herein, and that such 
consent will be memorialized in a notice recorded with the Navajo County Recorder 
to notify future owners of the affected property that sound levels may exceed the 
sound levels specifie d herein. The consent shall include a legal description of the 
affected property. A copy of each such consent on which the permit/agreement 
holder relies shall be submitted prior to approval of the permit/agreement. 
 
3. All wind turbine operations shall meet the operational low-frequency noise requirements 
applicable to wind turbines as specified in Noise Requirement Guidelines adopted, 
published and amended from time to time by the Board of Supervisors. 
 
4. Background and Compliance Testing: The requirements of subparagraph a above require 
that background (predevelopment) sound levels be properly assessed, that sound levels 
be forecast in advance of permit/agreement approval, and that, once a project commences 
operation, sound levels again be assessed as part of compliance-period assessment. Before 
a permit/agreement is issued, the applicant’s independent consultant shall complete a 
sound evaluation by determining existing (pre -project) background sound levels and 
forecasting ambient sound levels anticipated upon completion of the facility. The 
evaluation shall addres s facility aging and planned or probable modifications. If the 
project is permitted and constructed, w hen it is in operation the permit/agreement 
holder’s independent consultant shall complete a compliance -period sound evaluation. 
Background and post -construction compliance sound measurements shall comply with 
Noise Requirement Guidelines adopted, published and amended from time to time by the 
Board of Supervisors. If there is any conflict between the requirements of this ordinance 
and the requirements of such guidelines, the more stringent requirement(s) shall control. 
For phased/staged development, background sound levels shall be determined before the 
initial phase of the project. For a situation in which multiple developments by the same 
or multiple developers are expected in an area, the same applies.

<!-- page 779 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   50 
 
5. During the first three months of facility operation and more specifically during a period 
of normal full production operations, the SUP holder shall verify compliance with 
subparagraph a above utilizing an independent consultant. If operational sound is found 
to exceed the limits specified in subparagraph a above, the SUP holder shall institute 
remedies to achieve compliance with the applicable limits, or submit a consent from each 
owner of an affected property in accordance with subparagraph b above. Durin g the 
remedy period the SUP holder shall identify and remove from service the equipment 
responsible for the excessive sound until the problem can be cured or mitigated. Navajo 
County staff may require additional compliance testing when deemed appropriate. 
 
6. Plans for determining background sound levels and for modeling/simulation shall be 
submitted by the applicant for the P lanning and Development Services  Department’s 
review and approval in advance of the work. 
 
7. Setbacks. The minimum safety setback distance, location and spacing requirements for 
Wind Energy Generation facilities shall be as follows. As used herein, “total tower height” 
means the height from grade to the top of the structure, including the uppermos t 
extension of any blade (i.e., “straight up”). 
 
a. Wind towers shall be placed in accordance with the greater of the applicable 
setback and location requirements set forth in paragraphs A, B, and C below:  
 
i.  Such that the sound standards established in subparagraph b of this 
Section will not be exceeded.  
 
ii. Setbacks related to areas outside the project boundary: 
 
1)  Setback to existing residence: Individual wind towers shall be placed 
within the project boundary at least ½ -mile (2,640 feet) from an 
existing residence that is located outside of the project boundary.  
2) Setback to adjacent privately -owned land that is not zoned Industrial 
(I-1 or I-2):  
 
a) Parcels greater than 2.5 acres in size: Individual wind towers 
shall be placed within the project boundary at least ¼ -mile 
(1,320 feet) or 150% of the total tower height (whichever is 
greater) from the common property line with such parcels.  
 
b) Parcels 2.5 acres or smaller in size: Individual wind towers shall 
be placed within the project boundary at least ½ -mile (2,640 
feet) or 150% of the total tower height (whichever is greater) 
from the common property line with such parcels.  
 
Adjacent parcel sizes as set forth in paragraphs 1-2 above shall 
be determined as of the effective date of this Section.

<!-- page 780 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   51 
 
c) All other adjacent land not included in one of the foregoing 
categories: Individual wind towers shall be placed at least 1.1 
times (110%) the total tower height from the project boundary. 
 
iii. Setbacks related to areas within or outside the project boundary:  
 
1) Roadway (public or publicly-maintained): Individual wind towers shall 
be set back from any public or publicly -maintained roadway (as 
measured to the nearest edge of the right-of-way) at least ¼-mile (1,320 
feet).  
 
2) Railways, utility lines, interior phase lines and structures: Individual 
wind towers shall be set back from any railway (as measured to the 
nearest edge of the right -of-way), or from any utility line (above or 
below ground - as measured to the nearest edge of the utility easement), 
or from any interior phase line or structure (regardless of use), at least 
1.5 times (150%) the total tower height. 
 
a) The minimum setbacks from the project boundary for all non-
tower uses and structures (such as administrative buildings, 
meteorological or anemometer towers, maintenance 
buildings, operations buildings, transformers, etc.) shall 
conform to the setback requi rements for the Zoning District 
in which the use or structure is located. 
 
a. A reduction in the setback requirements set forth above in accordance with any or 
a combination of the following circumstances is allowed: 
 
i. The project shares a common property line with another approved Wind 
Energy Generation facility.  
 
ii. An irrevocable written consent from an affected property owner has been 
obtained, stating that the owner is aware of the proposed facility and the 
setback requirements imposed by this section, that consent is granted to 
allow lesser setbacks than those specified herein, and that such consent will 
be memorialized in a notice recorded with the Navajo County Recorder to 
notify future owners of the subject property that setbacks are less than 
those specified herein.  
 
iii. An adjacent property owner who is also pursuing the development of a 
Wind Energy Generation facility or similar use has filed a letter of consent 
to the proposed setback reduction with the Public Works Department.  
 
iv. The parcel on which the project is located and an adjacent parcel are held 
in common ownership.

<!-- page 781 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   52 
 
v. The current use of an adjacent property generates sound in excess of that 
permissible for the Wind Energy Generation facility under the terms of this 
section. 
 
b. Setback areas may be used for access within the development but are otherwise to 
remain in their current vegetative state. 
 
8. Wind Energy Generation projects shall comply with applicable Federal Aviation 
Administration (FAA) lighting, navigation and other requirements. Lighting shall be the 
minimum required by FAA regulations or other public safety considerations. The use of 
low-intensity, red pulsating/blinking lighting is preferred so long as consistent with FAA 
regulations. The use of strobes and strobe -type lighting for nighttime use is prohibited 
unless specifically required by the FAA. All lighting shall be in compliance with the Navajo 
County Lighting Ordinance. 
 
9. Wind Energy Generation facility projects shall comply with applicable Federal 
Communication Commission (FCC) requirements, including those applicable to 
microwave communication links in the vicinity. Wind Energy Generation facilities shall 
minimize and mit igate telecommunication interference (electromagnetic fields and 
communications interference generated by the project). No interference with public 
communication systems shall be allowed. 
 
10. Towers, generator housings, hubs and blades shall be painted a non-reflective, unobtrusive 
color which shall complement the surrounding landscape, including but not limited to 
white, off-white, beige or tan. The design of other buildings and other structur es shall, to 
the extent reasonably feasible and consistent with public safety, use materials, colors, 
textures, screening and landscaping that will blend the facility into the existing 
environment 
 
11. The applicant shall avoid locating turbines in mountain passes or draws or on cliff edges in 
order to minimize avian and/or bat collisions when wildlife studies show that the project 
would pose a significant risk to avian and/or bat populations. Towers and nacelles shall be 
designed so as not to attract nesting birds or serve as perches for raptors. The SUP holder 
shall refer to the Arizona Game and Fish Department’s and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife 
Services’ wind guidelines that have been developed to aid th e project proponents in 
reducing impacts to wildlife. 
 
12. Pre-construction and post-construction wildlife studies shall be developed and performed 
with consideration given to the Arizona Game and Fish Department and U.S. Fish and 
Wildlife Service guidelines. Any wildlife impacts discovered during formal post -
construction surveys shall be identified in the formal annual report submitted to the 
Arizona Game and Fish Department and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, with a copy to the 
Planning and Development Services Department. The formal annual report shall include 
avian and bat deaths due to the project.  All wind towers must be designed and constructed, 
to the greatest extent feasible, so as to prevent interior/exterior access by the public and 
shall have interior ladders and locking doors. 
 
13. Wind turbine designs with blades downwind of the tower are prohibited.

<!-- page 782 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   53 
 
Section 1203 – Solar Energy Generation Facilities 
The following provisions shall be specific for the review of Solar Energy Generation Facilities: 
1. Setbacks. All Solar Energy Generation Facilities and structures must comply with setback, 
building height, and performance standards between zones for the zoning district in which 
the system is located, unless the County determines a modified setback is necessary to 
address impacts to existing adjacent uses. 
   
2. A reduction in the setback requirements set forth above in accordance with any or a 
combination of the following circumstances is allowed: 
 
a. The project shares a common property line with another approved Solar Energy 
Generation facility.  
 
b. An irrevocable written consent from an affected property owner has been 
obtained, stating that the owner is aware of the proposed facility and the 
setback requirements imposed by this section, that consent is granted to allow 
lesser setbacks than those spe cified herein, and that such consent will be 
memorialized in a notice recorded with the Navajo County Recorder to notify 
future owners of the subject property that setbacks are less than those specified 
herein.  
 
3. Buffering.  Solar Energy Generation Facilities that adjoin residential development shall be 
required to provide adequate screening through the use of fences, walls, landscaping, or 
other structures deemed adequate by Planning and Development Services. 
Section 1204 – Fees 
Fees for Special Use Permits for Renewable Energy Generation Facilities shall be $600.00 plus 
$50.00 per acre, with a fee cap of $25,000.00.

<!-- page 783 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   54 
 
ARTICLE 13 – WIRELESS COMMUNICATION FACILITIES 
Section 1301 – Purpose  
The purpose of this Section is to establish rules and regulations for the siting of wireless 
communications facilities. The goals of this Section are to provide for the development of wireless 
communication services County-wide by:  
1. Considering the public health, safety, and welfare.  
 
2. Considering impact on adjacent properties.  
 
3. Encouraging configuration which minimizes additional visual impact through proper 
siting, design, landscape, and camouflage techniques.  
 
4. Considering historical and environmentally sensitive areas.  
 
5. Encouraging the collocation of facilities. 
Section 1302 – Applicability 
All wireless communications facilities requiring a Special Use Permit shall be subject to this 
Section except those used by a single user and not otherwise restricted within that Zoning District, 
including, but not limited to, radio and devices necessary f or the use of a subscription to a 
commercial wireless provider service such as wireless internet and satellite TV. 
Section 1303 – General Provisions 
The following provisions are applicable to all wireless communication requests requiring a Special 
Use Permit: 
1. Principal or Accessory Use: Antennas and towers may be considered either principal or 
accessory uses to the principal use of the property. 
 
2. Lot Size: For purposes of determining whether the installation of a tower or antenna 
complies with the applicable zoning district regulations, even though the antennas or 
towers may be located on a separately leased portion of the lot, the zoning district 
requirements of the entire overall lot shall control requirements, including, but not 
limited to, setbacks, lot-coverage percentages, and other such requirements. 
 
3. Wireless Communications Facility Characteristics: 
 
a. Wireless communication facilities including the tower structure, antennae, and 
related electrical and mechanical equipment, shall use materials, colors, textures,  
screening, and landscaping to minimize their visual impact on the natural and 
surrounding setting, unless subject to applicable standards of the FAA. 
 
b. Towers shall not be lighted, unless required by the FAA or other applicable 
authority. If lighting is required by the FAA or other authorities, all effort shall be 
taken to minimize light pollution.

<!-- page 784 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   55 
 
 
c. All wireless communication facilities shall maintain compliance with applicable 
State or local building codes under which they were constructed and any 
regulations of the FAA, the FCC, and any other federal government agency with the 
authority to regulate them or their components. Should applicable federal 
standards and regulations change, the n the owner(s) of the wireless 
communication facilities shall bring their facilities into compliance within three (3) 
months of the effective date of the updated standards. Wireless communications 
facilities that are not in compliance shall be removed at t he owner's expense if not 
brought into compliance within thirty (30) days after written demand by Navajo 
County. 
 
d. The following setback requirements shall apply to all towers within the appropriate 
classification: 
 
i. Residential: Towers must be set back two feet (2’) from any lot line for each 
one foot (1’) in height of the tower, including tower and antenna 
attachments. 
 
ii. Non-Residential: Towers must be set back one foot (1’) from any lot line for 
each one foot (1’) in height of the tower, including tower and antenna 
attachments. 
 
e. The following height requirements shall apply to all towers within the appropriate 
classification: 
 
i. Residential: The maximum height of a wireless communications facility, 
including the base, platform, and attached antennae shall not exceed eighty 
feet (80’) above grade. 
 
ii. Non-residential: The maximum height of a wireless communications 
facility, including the base, platform, and attached antennae shall not 
exceed one hundred ninety-nine feet (199’) above grade. 
 
f. Wireless communication structures in excess of one hundred ninety -nine feet 
(199’) in height are prohibited unless collocating on an existing structure (other 
than a wireless communication facility tower) and unless there is a plan to mitigate 
interference with military and commercial aircraft, disruption of avian migration 
and nesting, and to preserve nighttime skies for astronomical observation. Such 
wireless communication structures in excess of one hundred ninety-nine feet (199’) 
shall be required to obtain Variance approval of the Board of Adjustment. 
 
g. Accessory structures are subject to the applicable Zoning District setback 
requirements. 
 
h. Facilities that are located on existing or replaced streetlights, traffic signal poles, or 
electrical utility poles are exempt from any setback requirements.

<!-- page 785 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   56 
 
i. Setback and separation distances shall be applicable irrespective of municipal and 
County jurisdictional boundaries. 
 
j. No signs shall be permitted at a wireless communications facility with the exception 
of a single, one (1) square foot sign for each carrier, to provide emergency contact 
numbers. 
 
k. Except as provided in this Section, all use and development standards, including 
height restrictions, within the applicable Zoning District shall apply to wireless 
communication facilities. 
 
l. Equipment shall not generate noise levels that exceed fifty (50) dBA Sound 
Pressure Level (SPL) on directly adjacent properties. This noise requirement does 
not apply to generators used in emergency situations should the regular power 
supply be temporarily disrupted, and noise made during the regular maintenance 
and upkeep of the facility and site. All aboveground, accessory equipment shall be 
enclosed by concrete masonry unit walls if located within three hundred feet (300’) 
of existing residences. 
 
m. All components of a wireless communication facility shall be at least thirty (30) feet 
away from any travelled lane or shall be protected by a physical barrier such as a 
block wall, concrete wall, etc. if a lesser distance is requested. 
 
n. No wireless communication facilities shall be allowed in a floodway. 
Section 1303 – Performance Criteria 
New facilities shall use the most preferred facility type where technically feasible, even if it results 
in an increase in the number of facilities, or a higher cost. A lesser preferred facility type may be 
permitted only if the applicant presents substantial evidence to show that it will have a lesser visual 
impact than the use of more preferred facilities. The order of preference for new facilities is as 
follows (from most preferred to least preferred): 
1. Collocation on an existing facility or electrical utility pole. 
 
2. Attached antennas on an existing structure. 
 
3. New sites located on public lands at least three hundred feet (300’) from private land. 
 
4. New concealed, disguised, or attached antenna sites located on/at public or quasi -public 
facilities. 
 
5. Concealed/Stealth antennas. 
 
6. New towers/facilities suitable for collocating multiple providers. 
 
7. New towers/facilities under ninety-nine feet (99’). 
 
8. New towers/facilities one hundred feet (100’) to one hundred ninety-nine feet (199’).

<!-- page 786 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   57 
 
Section 1304 – Wireless Communications Facilities as a Permitted Use 
Wireless communications facilities located on property owned, leased, or controlled by Navajo 
County pursuant to agreement of, or approved by, Navajo County or any other governmental 
agency shall be a permitted use in all Zoning Districts with Zoning Clear ance. Towers on these 
properties should follow Special Use Permit setback guidelines as much as practicable. Prior to 
entering into a lease agreement with Navajo County or a governmental agency, the potential lessee 
shall conduct an informational meeting for owners of property within three hundred feet (300’) of 
the proposed facility. If a community/homeowners’ association is within three hundred feet 
(300’), they shall also be notified of this meeting. 
Section 1305 – Application Review 
1. General. The following provisions shall govern the issuance of permits for towers or 
antennas: 
 
a. If a wireless communication facility is not a permitted use, then Special Use Permit 
approval shall be required for the construction. 
 
b. Applicants shall submit an engineering analysis with a written narrative confirming 
the structural stability of an antenna/tower, its foundation, and any attachments, 
connections, or accessories. This analysis shall be certified by an Arizona licensed 
professional engineer as being in conformance with the current adopted code by 
Navajo County for structural towers. 
 
c. The Director is authorized to employ, on behalf of the County, an independent 
technical expert to review any technical materials submitted including, but not 
limited to, those required under this section and in those cases where a technical 
demonstration o f unavoidable need or unavailability of alternatives is required. 
The applicant shall pay all the costs of said review. 
 
d. Prior to applying for a new facility, the applicant shall meet with community groups 
and interested individuals who reside or own property within three hundred feet 
(300’) of the proposed site to describe and detail the proposed project. The purpose 
of the se meetings is to inform and educate the community on wireless 
communications, and the restrictions placed on Navajo County by the Federal 
Telecommunications Act of 1996, as well as to solicit suggestions from these groups 
about the applicant’s proposal and impact mitigation measures. The applicant shall 
make a concerted effort to incorporate the community suggestions for impact 
mitigation generated by the meetings and describe the efforts in the application. 
The applicant shall be prepared to discuss infor mation including, but not limited 
to, technical aspects, visual aspects, including alternative sites and designs. The 
applicant shall provide detailed meeting minutes, copy of all materials delivered or 
received, and documentation of who attended the meetings.

<!-- page 787 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   58 
 
2. Application Requirements. The following is to be submitted with each Special Use Permit 
application: 
 
a. A completed Special Use Permit application packet. 
 
b. Plans showing elevation drawings of the exterior of each element of the proposed 
wireless communication facility, method of fencing, coloration, and landscaping. 
 
c. The setback distance between the proposed wireless communication facility the 
nearest residential unit and/or the nearest residential zoned privately owned 
properties. 
 
d. A map showing the adjacent roadways and proposed means of legal access.  
 
e. Copies of all wireless telecommunication licenses for all providers who will use the 
facility at the time of filing the application. 
 
f. Copy of signed, redacted, lease agreement with landowner. 
 
g. Certification of whether the applicant is applying for collocation treatment, and 
how many carriers could be accommodated on the facility with adequate signal 
coverage. 
 
h. Attendees list, minutes, and information obtained from required community 
meeting. 
 
i. Certification that no Navajo County or municipal owned site, or existing wireless 
facility reasonably meets the needs of the applicant, listing all such sites within five 
(5) miles of the proposed site and the reason each is not physically adequate for 
reasonable commercial coverage, or not economically feasible for location. 
 
j. A visual analysis, which may include photo simulations, field mockups, or other 
techniques which identify the potential visual impacts of the proposed facility. 
Photo simulations shall be provided from the five (5) closest residences within two 
(2) miles of the proposed site and from the closest collector or arterial street. The 
Development Services Director may, at their discretion, request additional photos 
from specific vantage points. 
 
k. A written narrative/explanation of why it is necessary that the proposed wireless 
communications facility be located in the proposed location, and why it will exceed 
the maximum height allowance for the Zoning District in which it is proposed. If 
the explanation is based on coverage maps, structural calculations, lease amounts, 
or any other information pertinent to the need for the structure or additional 
height, this information shall be included as appendices to the narrative.

<!-- page 788 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   59 
 
3. Standards. I n addition to any standards for consideration of Special Use Permit 
applications, the following shall be considered in determining whether to issue a Special 
Use Permit: height proposed, proximity to other uses, historic sites, landmarks, vehicle 
traffic r outes, medical facilities, air routes, topographical features, utilities, access, 
suitability of alternative sites and visual impact. 
Section 1306 – Collocation 
The purpose of this Section is to encourage collocation. 
1. An applicant who certifies in writing that the tower constructed will be suitable for 
collocating multiple providers of varying wireless technologies and, as a condition of 
zoning, executes a written agreement (collocation agreement) with Navajo County, 
consenting to application of the terms of this provision shall, unless waived by the 
applicant have their request considered more preferred as outlined in Performance 
Criteria. 
 
2. In addition to equipment proposed for the applicant’s use, proposed antenna facilities, 
including concealed antennas, shall be designed to accommodate collocation for at least 
one (1) additional wireless communications provider for every thirty foot (30’) segment 
of facility height, or portion thereof, over thirty feet (30’). The Board of Supervisors may 
reduce the required shared capacity, if a facility necessary to provide for such collocation 
adversely alters the area’s visual character. 
 
3. Collocation Agreement. The collocation agreement shall provide for at least the following: 
 
a. The applicant shall accept for collocation any FCC licensed wireless communication 
provider (additional user) using any compatible technology on commercially 
reasonable terms considering all of the factors a reasonable tower leasing company 
would deem relevant in entering into such an agreement. 
 
b. Any additional user seeking collocation shall submit specifications for its 
equipment and use (request) to the applicant and applicant shall, within thirty (30) 
days thereafter, respond to such party in writing (response) furnishing all technical 
requirements that must be resolved before collocation. 
 
c. The applicant and the additional user shall, thereafter, attempt to resolve any 
technical or business terms. If, after thirty (30) days from the response, the 
additional user believes the applicant has not negotiated in good faith, additional 
user may submit in writing, a request for arbitration to applicant and the American 
Arbitration Association which shall designate a person knowledgeable in 
collocation of wireless communication carriers to act as arbitrator and decide all 
issues between the parties. Such arbitration shall be held within thirty (30) days of 
the request for arbitration. Upon the written agreement of both parties, a different 
procedure for binding dispute resolution may be used. The result of the arbitration 
or other resolution method agre ed to by the parties shall be binding and non -
appealable.

<!-- page 789 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   60 
 
d. If the arbitrator certifies in writing to Navajo County that the applicant has failed 
to comply with the decision of the arbitrator within fifteen (15) days of its issuance 
by the arbitrator, the Special Use Permit for the wireless communication facility in 
question shall be terminated and the wireless communications facility shall be 
removed within thirty (30) days of the date of the arbitrator's certification, failing 
which, Navajo County shall have all of the remedies available to it for elimination 
of a use in violation of the zoning code. 
 
e. The additional party, upon submitting the request shall become a third -party 
beneficiary to the collocation agreement. 
 
f. Navajo County shall not be a party to any contract between the applicant and the 
additional party and shall not be a required party and shall not be made a party to 
any dispute or arbitration and applicant shall indemnify, defend, and hold Navajo 
County harmless from any cost, including reasonable attorney fees, associated with 
such matters. 
 
g. A lease or other agreement containing the business terms proposed by the applicant 
for collocation shall be attached as an exhibit to the collocation agreement. 
Section 1307 – Removal 
1. Within thirty (30) days of Board of Supervisors approval, financial assurances shall be 
posted by the applicant for the occurrence or possible need for removal of the tower and 
returning the natural state of the site, prior to submittal and approval of bui lding 
permits/zoning clearances. 
 
2. Towers and antennae shall be removed, at the owner’s expense, within one hundred eighty 
(180) days if not used for a permanent use within that time unless this period is extended 
pursuant to this Section. If the tower or antennae is not timely removed Nava jo County 
may give notice that it will contract for removal within thirty (30) days following written 
notice to the owner. Thereafter, Navajo County may cause removal at the cost of the 
owner. 
 
3. An owner wishing to extend the time for removal or reactivation shall submit an 
application stating the reason for such extension. The Director or their designate may 
extend the time for removal or reactivation up to sixty (60) additional days upon a showing 
of good cause. 
 
4. Upon removal of the wireless telecommunications facility, the site shall be returned to its 
natural state and topography and vegetated consistent with the natural surroundings.

<!-- page 790 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   61 
 
Section 1308 – Modification 
No existing wireless telecommunications facility may be changed or modified  without a Special 
Use Permit Amendment, except if it meets all of the following criteria: 
1. The change does not substantially change the physical dimensions of the wireless 
communication tower or base station. 
 
2. The modification submitted shall be sealed by an Arizona Licensed professional engineer 
to certify that it meets all safety standards for structural stability and is in conformance 
with the current adopted code by Navajo County for structural towers.

<!-- page 791 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   62 
 
ARTICLE 14 – HEARING PROCESSES 
Section 1401 – Purpose  
The main purpose of this Article is to provide information on public hearing processes initiated 
through the Planning and Development Services Department.  This Article provides for required 
hearings in front of the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commis sion (Commission), Navajo 
County Board of Adjustment, and Navajo County Board of Supervisors (Board). 
Section 1402 – Authority 
1. The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission shall serve in an advisory capacity 
to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, supplying reports and recommendations after 
public hearings required by law on amendments to Zoning District boundaries or the 
regulations herein or subsequently established.  Amendment may be initiated either by 
application or by the Commission on its own motion. 
 
2. The Navajo County Board of Supervisors may, after receiving report and recommendation 
thereupon by the Commission and after public hearings required by law, amend Zoning 
District boundaries or the regulations herein or subsequently established.   
 
3. All items that qualify for public hearing processes in front of the Planning and Zoning 
Commission and Board of Supervisors shall be able to enter into a Development 
Agreement with Navajo County, pursuant to A.R.S. § 11-1101.  These Development 
Agreements may be in lieu of required hearing processes, or in combination, as deemed 
appropriate by Navajo County.  
 
4. The Navajo County Board of Adjustment may: 
 
a. Interpret the Zoning Ordinance if the meaning of any word, phrase, or section is in 
doubt, if there is dispute between the appellant and Director, or if the location of a 
District boundary is in doubt. 
 
b. Allow a variance from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance if, owing to peculiar 
conditions, a strict interpretation would work an unnecessary hardship and if in 
granting the variance, the general intent and purposes of the Zoning Ordinance will 
be preserved. 
Section 1403 – Amendments Initiated by Petition 
1. Any owner or owners of property desiring an amendment to Zoning District boundaries 
or the regulations herein or subsequently established, shall file with the Department an 
application, duly signed and acknowledged, describing the proposed amendments, 
supplements, or change of the regulation of this Ordinance or Zoning District boundaries.  
Each application shall be accompanied by a map showing the existing and proposed 
District boundaries and other information relating thereto, and by the fee prescribed by  
the Navajo County Board of Supervisors.

<!-- page 792 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   63 
 
2. Upon acceptance of a complete application, the Department shall submit the application 
to the Commission for report and recommendation.  Prior to providing its report and 
recommendation to the Board, the Commission shall hold a public hearing on such 
application in compliance with A.R.S. §§ 11-813 or 11-814, whichever is applicable to the 
application received. 
 
3. Upon receiving the report and recommendation of the Commission, the Board of 
Supervisors shall hold a public hearing on such application in compliance with A.R.S. §§ 
11-813 or 11-814, whichever is applicable to the application received. 
Section 1404 – Amendments Initiated by the Commission. 
Amendments initiated by the Commission are subject to the same public hearing requirements 
outlined in A.R.S. §§ 11-813 and 11-814.  
Section 1405 – Board of Supervisors Adoption of Amendments Without a Second 
Public Hearing 
Pursuant to A.R.S. § 11 -814 and this Zoning Ordinance, the Board of Supervisors, following a 
public hearing by the Planning and Zoning Commission may adopt the recommendations of the 
Commission through use of consent calendar without holding a second publi c hearing, provided 
there is no objection, request for public hearing, or other protest. 
Section 1406 – Citizen Review 
1. Citizen Review Plan: All processes that require a hearing in front of the Navajo County 
Planning and Zoning Commission shall require a Citizen Review Plan from the applicant, 
developed in consultation with Planning and Development Services Staff. This Plan shall 
include the following: 
 
a. A draft letter or notice of a Neighborhood Community Meeting, with any relevant 
written material. The letter or notice shall notify residents and public agencies who 
may be affected by the application of the substance of the request proposed in the 
application. This letter shall be reviewed by Planning and D evelopment Services 
Staff, prior to mailing. 
 
b. Interested and affected parties will be provided an opportunity to discuss the 
applicant’s proposal with the applicant and express any concerns, issues, or 
problems they may have with the proposal at a Neighborhood Community Meeting, 
which shall be conducted prior to any hearing. 
 
c. A mailing list of residents and public agencies who will receive the invitation. This 
list can either be prepared by the applicant and reviewed by Planning and 
Development Services Staff or generated by Planning and Development Services 
Staff.

<!-- page 793 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   64 
 
2. Neighborhood Community Meeting: Applicants for a process requiring a hearing in front 
of the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission must conduct a Neighborhood 
Community meeting, which shall meet the following requirements: 
 
a. The meeting may be conducted on -site, in the general vicinity of the subject 
property, or virtually, subject to the approval of the Director, or their designee. This 
meeting shall serve as a medium for information exchange between applicants and 
affected members of the public, prior to the required public hearing. 
 
b. Notice of this meeting shall be sent to all owners, as shown on the last assessment 
whose property is located within three -hundred feet (300’) of the boundary of the 
subject property; and all persons who, in the judgement of the Director, or their 
designee, after consideration of the nature of the application and the location and 
character of the subject property, will be affected by the application. 
 
i. The Director’s, or designee’s, judgement as to the persons affected by the 
proposed application, or failure of any person to receive notice, shall not be 
a basis for challenging or invalidating the approval or denial of that 
application. 
 
c. Affected members of the public shall be noticed in writing of a Neighborhood 
Community Meeting not less than fifteen (15) days prior to said meeting. 
 
d. An applicant may make a written request and receive a written determination 
whether, due to impractical circumstances, such as a site surrounded by State or 
federal lands, the requirement for a Neighborhood Community Meeting may be 
waived by the Director, or their designee. This request must explain why the 
applicant’s Citizen Review Plan provides other adequate, alternative opportunities 
for citizens to express any concerns, problems, or issues they may have with the 
proposal in advance of the public hearing. 
 
3. Citizen Review Plan Report: Applicants shall provide a written report on the results of 
their Citizen Review Plan. This Citizen Review Plan Report shall include the following 
information: 
 
a. Dates and locations of all meetings where citizens were invited to discuss the 
proposal. 
 
b. Content, dates mailed, numbers of mailings, including letters, meeting notices, 
newsletters, and other written material. 
 
c. The address list of residents and parties notified, as well as written materials. 
 
d. A sign-in sheet from the Neighborhood Community Meeting, listing the name and 
number of people that participated in the process.

<!-- page 794 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   65 
 
e. A written summary of concerns, issues, and problems expressed during the process, 
which are to include: 
 
i. How the applicant has addressed or intends to address concerns, issues, 
and problems expressed during the process; or 
 
ii. Concerns, issues, and problems that the applicant is unwilling or unable to 
address and why. 
Section 1407 – Board of Adjustment 
1. Applications for variance shall include, at a minimum: 
 
a. An accurate site plan and description of the property 
 
b. Reasons for requesting the variance. 
 
2. Applications for interpretation of the Zoning Ordinance shall include, at a minimum: 
 
a. Letter identifying the section of the Ordinance for which the interpretation is 
requested and explaining how the applicant believes the section should be 
interpreted. 
 
b. If the application involves a dispute with the Director, the letter shall also explain 
the Director’s interpretation and how it differs from the applicant’s.  In such cases, 
the application shall be filed within thirty (30) days after the applicant has received 
the Director’s interpretation in writing.  The filing of the application shall stay any 
further action based on the Director’s interpretation unless the Director certifies in 
writing to the Board of Adjustment that stay would cause imminent peril to life or 
property; in such cases, further action shall not be stayed unless the applicant 
obtains an injunction from a court of competent jurisdiction.  
 
3. Upon acceptance of a complete application for interpretation of the Zoning Ordinance or 
variance, the Department shall submit the application to the Board for report and 
decision.  Prior to providing its report and decision, the Board shall hold a public hearing 
on such application in compliance with A.R.S. § 11-816. 
Section 1408 – Appeals  
Any person aggrieved in any manner by an action of the Planning and Zoning Commission, Board 
of Supervisors, or Board of Adjustment for a process described within this Article may appeal 
within thirty (30) days to the superior court, and the matter shall be heard de novo.  A copy of the 
appeal document, as filed in the superior court, shall be served on the Director within the same 
thirty (30) day period by personal service or mail.  Personal service includes delivery to a 
responsible person in the Departme nt at its office in Show Low.  Service by mail is complete on 
mailing.

<!-- page 795 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   66 
 
Section 1409 – Reconsideration of Denied Petition 
If an application for amendment is denied by the Board of Supervisors, that application shall not 
be refiled, nor shall there be any other application filed with the Department for the same 
amendment within one (1) year unless there is a change of circumstances warranting such filing.   
Section 1410 – Fees  
Unless a different amount is expressly stated elsewhere in the Zoning Ordinance, the fees for 
amendments and variances shall be in accordance with a published schedule of fees adopted by 
the Board of Supervisors, which may be amended from time to time.  Th ere shall be no fee for 
filing an application for interpretation of the Zoning Ordinance.

Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   67 
 
ARTICLE 15 – RECREATIONAL VEHICLE PLACEMENT (RV) 
Section 1501 – Purpose 
The purpose of this Article is to allow the temporary placement of a Recreational Vehicle (RV), 
while protecting the environmental, aesthetic, and quality of life values of Navajo County.  This 
Article regulates the placement of an RV outside of an approve d RV Park.  This Article does not 
regulate the placement of an RV within the boundaries of an approved RV Park, National Forest, 
National Park, State Park, or County Park.  This Article provides for the temporary placement of 
an RV .  
Section 1502 – General Provisions 
1. The placement of a single RV is allowed, subject to compliance with the other provisions 
of this Article, in the following Zoning Districts only: A -General, Rural (RU), Single-
Family (R1) and Special Development (if approval of development provides for RV 
placement). 
2. An RV shall not be placed in the following Zoning Districts: Industrial (IND), 
Commercial-Residential (C -R), or Multi -Family (R), except in an approved RV Park.  
However, the Director may, on a case -by-case basis, waive this restriction to grant a 
Temporary RV Permit for placement in any of these Zoning Districts upon a showing of 
good cause. 
3. No RV shall be placed on a permanent basis.  
4. No RV shall be placed as a rental unit. 
5. The placement of an RV in violation of Deed Restrictions or Covenants, Conditions, and 
Restrictions (CC&Rs) is discouraged.  However, Deed Restrictions and CC&Rs are private 
matters between the owners of the parcels to which they apply.  Enforcement is not  the 
responsibility of Navajo County.  
6. The placement of an RV is subject to all zoning regulations, including setbacks, applicable 
to the parcel on which the RV is placed.  In addition to the setback requirements, the RV 
shall be placed an additional ten feet from all property lines.  
7. The placement of an RV is subject to the Navajo County Floodplain Ordinance.  A separate 
Floodplain Use Permit may be required from the Flood Control District (Department of 
Public Works).  
8. Solid waste (garbage) and sewage shall be disposed of in an approved system and are 
subject to all applicable Department regulations. 
9. RVs shall be connected to a permanent power source.  Usage of generators to power RVs 
is prohibited.  
10. No temporary or permanent site-built additions or improvements shall be attached to the 
RV.  Any structure such as snow shed, porch, deck, or carport shall be free -standing.  
Building Permits must be obtained, where required.

<!-- page 797 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   68 
 
11. The fee for a Temporary RV Permit shall be in accordance with a schedule of fees adopted 
by the Board of Supervisors.  
Section 1503 – Placement with Seasonal RV Permits 
Subject to the provisions of Section 1402, a single RV may be placed one time each calendar year, 
for a period not to exceed one hundred and twenty (120) days, upon acquiring a Seasonal RV 
Permit.  This Seasonal RV Permit may be renewed up to once per cale ndar year, upon a showing 
of good cause.  The fee for a Seasonal RV Permit shall be in accordance with a schedule of fees 
adopted by the Board of Supervisors.  
Section 1504 – Placement with Temporary RV Permits 
Subject to the provisions of Section 1402, a single RV may be placed for a period of up to one year 
upon the issuance of a Temporary RV (TRV) Permit, pursuant to this section.  The permit may be 
renewed, upon a showing of good cause.  
1. A TRV may be issued by the Director at the same time that a Building Permit is issued for 
the construction of a principal dwelling on the same parcel.  The TRV shall run with the 
Building Permit.  The TRV shall expire when the Building Permit expires, a Certificate of 
Occupancy is issued for the principal dwelling, or at the end of the one -year issuance, 
whichever comes first. 
2. A TRV may be obtained from the Director in circumstances other than in connection with 
the issuance of a Building Permit.  The Director shall determine, on a case -by-case basis, 
the merits of the request and may impose conditions.  
3. The Director may notify adjoining property owners of an application for a TRV in any 
reasonable manner and may solicit their comments prior to issuance of the permit.  The 
Director’s decisions as to whether the application warrants notice to adjoining prop erty 
owners, and as to the manner of such notice, shall be final.  
4. All utility hookups shall originate from the parcel on which the RV is placed.  Utilities 
shall be connected, subject to securing the appropriate permits. 
Section 1505 – Special Event Placement 
A TRV may be issued for the placement of one or more RVs in connection with the issuance of a 
Special Event Permit, pursuant to Section 1911 of this Ordinance.  The TRV shall be issued by the 
Director.  Conditions of this type of TRV may relate specifically to the Special Event.  There shall 
be a separate fee for the TRV.

2. Location of Required Parking Spaces: The required parking spaces shall in all cases be on

spaces when used together is not less than the sum of spaces required for the  various 
individual buildings or uses computed separately.

ARTICLE 17 – SIGNS 
Section 1701 – Prohibited Signs  
The following signs are prohibited under any circumstances: 
1. Signs extending into the public right-of-way.  
2. Roof signs. 
3. Strobe lights and rotating beacons – direct light. 
4. Signs that are similar in color, design, and appearance to traffic control signs.  
5. Vehicular signs. 
6. Any sign which emits audible sound, odor, smoke, steam, laser lights, hologram lights, or 
other visible matter, including any sign that employs motion picture projection. 
7. Signs with display lights that resemble flashing lights customarily associated with danger 
or those used by police, fire, ambulance, or other emergency vehicles. 
8. Other signs not expressly allowed by this Ordinance. 
Section 1702 - Signs not Requiring a Permit 
The following types of signs are exempted from permit requirements and allowed in all zones, but 
shall be in conformance with all other requirements of this ordinance: 
1. Plaques and grave markers. 
2. On-premises directional and instructional signs. 
3. Signs not exceeding two (2) square feet in area, attached to a building. 
4. Signs located on windows or glass doors that do not have a copy area exceeding fifty 
percent (50%) of the total window or glass door size.  
5. Flags and/or permanent poles. 
6. Signs that are in compliance with A.R.S. § 16-1019.  
7. Temporary signs, provided: 
a. One sign shall be allowed per property. 
b. Signs are not illuminated.  
c. Signs shall not exceed twenty-four (24) square feet in area.  
d. Signs are removed within ten (10) days after accomplishing their temporary 
purpose.

<!-- page 801 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   72 
 
Section 1703 - Sign Regulations – Single-Family Residential Properties 
Signs shall be permitted as follows: 
1. Such signs shall not exceed two (2) square feet in area. 
2. Such sign may be illuminated, but the source of illumination shall not be visible, and no 
flashing or intermittent illumination shall be employed. 
3. Such sign shall be placed flat against a wall of a building, but placement against a wall of 
a building shall be no higher than eight (8) feet above grade. 
4. Such sign shall be located on the property to which it pertains, and the number shall be 
limited to one (1) for each dwelling. 
Permanent directional signs, subject to the following: 
1. Such signs shall not exceed two (2) square feet in area. 
2. Such sign may be double-faced.  
3. Such sign may be illuminated, but the source of illumination shall not be visible, and no 
flashing or intermittent illumination shall be employed. 
4. Such sign may be placed flat against a wall of a building, or such sign may be free-standing.  
Placement against a wall of a building shall be no higher than eight (8) feet above grade. 
The height of a free-standing sign shall not exceed twelve (12) feet above ground. 
5. Such sign may be located in, or project into, required yards, but such sign shall not be 
located or project into any alley or street. 
Temporary directional signs, subject to the following: 
1. Such sign shall not exceed twelve (12) square feet in area. 
2. Such sign may be illuminated, but the source of illumination shall not be visible, and no 
flashing or intermittent illumination shall be employed. 
3. Such sign may be placed flat against a wall of a building, or such sign may be free-standing.  
Placement against a wall of a building shall be no higher than eight (8) feet above grade. 
The height of a free-standing sign shall not exceed twelve (12) feet above ground. 
4. Such sign may be located in, or project into, required yards, but such sign shall not be 
located or project into any alley or street. 
5. Such sign shall be removed from the property within ten (10) days after accomplishing 
the temporary purpose. 
Section 1704 - Sign Regulations – Multi-Family Residential Properties 
Signs shall be permitted as indicated within “Sign Regulations – Single-Family Residential 
Properties” or as follows: 
1. Such sign shall not exceed twenty-four (24) square feet in area.  
2. Such sign may be double-faced.

<!-- page 802 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   73 
 
3. Such sign may be illuminated, but the source of illumination shall not be visible, and no 
flashing or intermittent illumination shall be employed. 
4. Such sign may be placed flat against a wall of a building, or such sign may be free-standing.  
Placement against a wall of a building shall be no higher than twelve (12) feet above grade, 
nor above the roof line.  The height of a free -standing sign shall n ot exceed twelve (12)  
feet above grade. 
5. Such sign may be located in, or project into, required yards, but such sign shall not be 
located or project into any alley or street. 
6. Such sign shall be located on the property to which it pertains. 
Section 1705 - Sign Regulations – Commercial and Industrial Properties 
Signs shall be permitted as indicated within “Sign Regulations – Single-Family Residential 
Properties” or “Sign Regulations – Multi-Family Residential Properties” or as follows: 
1. Such sign shall not exceed an area of one square foot for each linear foot of street adjoining 
the property to which it pertains.  If multiple signs are proposed, the aggregate area of all 
signs shall also conform with these size requirements. 
a. Sign area need not be less than sixty (60) square feet, regardless of the adjoining length 
of street front. 
b. No sign shall exceed an area of one hundred fifty (150) square feet.  
2. Such sign(s) may be double-faced.  
3. Such sign may be illuminated, but the source of illumination shall not be visible, and no 
flashing or intermittent illumination shall be employed.  
4. Such sign may be attached to a wall of a building or may be free-standing. 
5. Such sign(s) shall not exceed a height of twenty-four feet (24’) above grade.  
6. Such sign may be located in or project into required yards, but such sign shall not be 
located or project into any alley or street.  
7. Electronic Message Displays are permitted, subject to the following: 
a. Electronic messages adjacent to a roadway with a speed limit of less than forty-five 
(45) miles per hour shall have a minimum of twenty (20) seconds between message 
change. 
b. Electronic messages adjacent to a roadway with a speed limit of forty-five (45) miles 
per hour or greater shall have a minimum of fifteen (15) seconds between message 
change. 
c. Electronic messages shall not contain flashing, blinking, fading, rolling, shading, 
dissolving, or any other effect that gives the appearance of movement. 
d. LED displays and lighting shall conform with Navajo County lighting standards. 
8. Such sign shall be located on the property to which it pertains.

Section 1706 - Sign Regulations – Outdoor Advertising Signs 
Outdoor Advertising Signs (Billboards) are required to be permitted, regardless of whether the 
billboard will be located in an area regulated by the Arizona Department of Transportation 
(ADOT), pursuant to the Highway Beautification Act, A.R.S. § 28-7901 et. seq.  
1. Billboards shall: 
 
a. Be located either: 
 
i. In the Commercial -Residential (C -R), IND -1 or IND -2 Zoning Districts 
along a highway which is part of the Interstate, Primary, or Secondary 
System, as evidenced by a permit issued by ADOT. 
 
ii. In the Commercial-Residential (C-R), IND-1, IND-2 Zoning Districts along 
a highway which has been established as a County Highway by the Board of 
Supervisors. 
 
b. Either: 
 
i. Meet the ADOT spacing requirements, if located along a highway that is 
part of the interstate system. 
 
ii. Be located at least one thousand feet (1000’) from any other billboard on 
the same side of the road and at least one -hundred feet (100’) from any 
freestanding on -premise sign, unless the sign is attached to the same 
supporting structure as the billboard. 
 
c. Not be located within one -half (1/2) mile of the corporate limits of any 
incorporated city or town (This applies to billboards approved after January 9, 
2001). 
 
d. Be a maximum of twenty-six feet (26’) in height above the road grade. 
 
e. Be a maximum of three-hundred twenty square feet (320 ft2 ) per side. 
 
i. If located along an Interstate Highway, up to six-hundred forty square feet 
(640 ft2) may be permitted. 
 
f. Not be located within one-thousand feet (1000’) of a Federal, State, County, or city 
park. 
 
g. Have a minimum of ten feet (10’) of vertical clearance. 
 
h. Submit with their application a survey prepared by a registered surveyor showing 
at least the following:

<!-- page 804 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   75 
 
i. The location of all outdoor advertising signs within one-thousand feet 
(1,000’) on the same side of the street and within five-hundred feet (500’) 
on the opposite side of the street. 
 
ii. Structures within twenty feet (20’). 
 
iii. Residential districts and institutional uses within five-hundred feet (500’). 
 
iv. Applicable setbacks and side or rear yards in the zoning district. 
 
i. Have any light source located at the top of the billboard, shielded in compliance 
with Navajo County lighting regulations and any applicable ADOT restrictions. 
 
j. Be maintained to applicable standards for structural integrity and safety and 
present a professional appearance. 
If a billboard fails to comply with any of the foregoing requirements, the Billboard Permit may be 
revoked by the Board of Supervisors pursuant to a recommendation by the Director. At least thirty 
(30) days before making such a recommendation to the Board, the Director shall deliver or mail a 
notice of noncompliance to the owner of the property on which the billboard is located. Such notice 
shall be delivered or mailed to the property owner at the curre nt address for property tax notices 
as shown in the rec ords of the County Assessor. If the billboard is separately taxed, a duplicate 
notice shall be delivered or mailed to the current address for tax notices as shown in the office of 
the County Assessor. The noncompliance may be cured at any time prior to the  effective date of 
revocation. If the noncompliance is not timely cured, the billboard shall be removed within thirty 
(30) days after the effective date of revocation. If the billboard is not timely removed, the Director 
may take appropriate enforcement action pursuant to Article 21 and/or Article 22 or may pursue 
any other available legal remedy.  
This Section shall not apply to billboards existing as of July 10, 2000, or to reasonable alterations 
or repairs thereof; provided, however, that such billboards shall be subject to all provisions of 
Article 20 hereof. 
Section 1707 - Additions to Sign Regulations  
1. Signs projecting or extending over streets shall be erected not less than eight feet  (8’) 
above any part of the sidewalk of such street. The projection or extension of signs over the 
vehicular lanes of streets shall not be permitted. Signs projecting or extending over alleys 
shall be not less than fifteen (15) feet above grade directly beneath such sign. 
 
2. Changing or replacing the permanent copy on an existing, lawful sign shall not require a 
permit, provided the copy change does not change the nature of the sign as to render the 
sign in violation of this Ordinance. 
 
3. All signs shall be maintained in good structural and aesthetic condition.  Deficiencies such 
as chipped paint, broken plastic, missing letters, and exposed lightbulbs shall be evidence 
of lack of maintenance.  If appropriate maintenance is not conducted, t he Director may 
take appropriate enforcement action pursuant to Article 21 and/or Article 22 of this 
Ordinance.

ARTICLE 18 – OUTDOOR LIGHTING  
Section 1801 – Purpose  
This ordinance is intended to encourage outdoor lighting practices and systems which prevent the 
impediment or impeding upon, or by, other citizens and provide for a more pristine nighttime 
environment free from light pollution, waste, trespass, or other c lutter while also providing for 
nighttime safety, security, and productivity. 
Section 1802 – General Provisions 
1. All outdoor artificial illuminating devices shall be installed in conformance with the 
provisions of this ordinance and any building ordinances or codes which may apply. 
Where any provisions of any of the Arizona State Statutes, or any of the federal law, or 
any companion ordinance comparatively conflicts with the requirements of this outdoor 
light control ordinance; the most restrictive shall govern. 
 
2. Preferred Source: Due to their high energy efficiency, long life, and spectral 
characteristics, low-pressure sodium (LPS) lights are currently the preferred illumination 
source throughout Navajo County. 
 
3. All outdoor light fixtures, including security lighting, except streetlamps, shall be aimed 
and shielded so that the direct illumination shall be confined to the property boundaries 
of the source. Particular care is to be taken to assure that the direct illumination does not 
fall onto or across any public or private street or road. 
Section 1803 – Prohibitions  
1. Searchlights: the operation of searchlights for advertising purposes is prohibited. 
 
2. Recreational Facility: no outdoor recreational facility, public or private, shall be 
illuminated by nonconforming means after 11:00 pm, except to conclude a specific 
recreational or sporting event or any other activity conducted at a ballpark, outdoor 
amphitheater, arena, or similar facility in progress prior to 11:00 pm. 
 
3. Outdoor Building or Landscaping Illumination: the unshielded outdoor illumination of 
any building, landscaping, signing or other purpose, is prohibited except with 
incandescent fixtures of less than 150 watts, or LED fixtures of less than 25 watts. 
 
4. Mercury Vapor: the installation of mercury vapor fixtures is prohibited. 
 
5. Light produced on a property shall not affect a neighboring property such that activities 
conducted on the neighboring property are adversely affected or experience unreasonable 
interference.

<!-- page 806 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   77 
 
Section 1804 – Permanent Exemptions 
1. Nonconforming Fixtures: All outdoor light fixtures existing and fully installed prior to the 
effective date of the ordinance may remain “nonconforming” indefinitely; provided, 
however, that no change in use, replacement, structural alteration, or restorati on, or 
substantial repair of such light fixtures shall be made unless it thereafter conforms to the 
provisions of these regulations. 
 
2. Fossil Fuel Light: Illumination produced directly or indirectly by the combustion of 
natural gas or other utility-type fossil fuels are exempt from this Ordinance. 
 
3. Federal and State Facilities: Those facilities and lands owned and/or operated as 
protected by the U.S. Federal Government or the State of Arizona are exempted by law 
from all requirements of this ordinance. In addition, all federal and state detention 
facilities and other places for lawful confinement shall have the same exemption. 
Voluntary compliance with the intent of this ordinance at those facilities is encouraged. 
 
4. Public and Private Detention Facilities: All detention facilities and other places for lawful 
confinement, whether they are public or private shall have the same exemptions as in 
paragraph 3. Voluntary compliance with the intent of this ordinance is encouraged. 
Section 1805 – Procedures for Ordinance Compliance 
1. Any individual applying for a building permit under the codes adopted by Navajo County 
intending to install outdoor lighting fixtures shall as a part of said application submit 
evidence that the proposed work will comply with this ordinance. 
 
2. Utility companies entering into a duly approved contract with Navajo County in which 
they agree to comply with the provisions of these regulations, shall be exempt from 
applying for and obtaining a permit for the installation of outdoor light fixtures, including 
residential security lighting. 
 
3. Contents of Application Submission: 
 
a. The submission shall contain, but shall not necessarily be limited to the following, 
all or part of which may be part of or in addition to the information required 
elsewhere in the Navajo County Building Codes and Zoning Ordinance upon 
application for the required permit: 
 
i. Plans indicating the location of the premises, and the type of illuminating 
devices, fixtures, lamps, supports, other devices, etc. 
 
ii. Description of the illuminating devices, fixtures, lamps, supports, and 
other devices, etc. this description may include, but is not limited to, 
manufacturer’s catalog cuts, and drawings (including sections where 
required).

<!-- page 807 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   78 
 
b. The above required plans and descriptions shall be sufficiently complete to enable 
the Chief Building Official to readily determine whether compliance with the 
requirements of this ordinance will be secured. If such plans and descriptions 
cannot enable this ready determination, by reason of the nature or configuration of 
the devices, fixtures or lamps proposed, the applicant shall submit evidence of 
compliance by certified test reports as performed by a recognized testing lab. 
 
4. Issuance of Permit: Upon compliance with the requirements of this ordinance, the Chief 
Building Official shall issue a permit for installation of the outdoor lighting fixture, to be 
installed as in the approved application. In the event the application is part of the building 
permit application under the building codes, the issuance of the building permit will be 
made if the applicant is in compliance with this ordinance as well as the other 
requirements for issuance under the regulations. 
 
5. Amendment to Permit: Should the applicant desire to substitute outdoor light fixtures or 
lamps after a permit has been issued, the applicant must submit all changes to the Chief 
Building Official for approval, with adequate information to assure compliance  with this 
ordinance.

ARTICLE 19 – GENERAL PROVISIONS 
Section 1901 – Applying General Provisions 
The regulations set forth in this Article qualify or supplement the Zoning District regulations 
appearing in this Ordinance. 
Section 1902 – Exempt Uses 
Nothing contained in this Ordinance shall restrict uses outlined in A.R.S. §§ 11-812, 820, 820.01, 
or 820.04. 
Section 1903 – General Development Review 
Developments as classified in A.R.S. § 11-269.27 may be reviewed and approved by Departmental 
administrative personnel in conjunction with this statute. 
Section 1904 – Accessory Buildings 
Accessory buildings may be built in the required rear or side setback but shall not be closer than 
five feet (5’) from any side or rear lot line.  Accessory buildings shall not be closer than ten feet 
(10’) from any street.   
Section 1905 – Number of Principal Buildings on a Lot 
Where a lot is located in Multiple-Family Residential, Commercial, or Industrial Zoning District, 
more than one (1) principal building may be located on the lot.  The location of these buildings 
shall conform to the setback requirements for the zoning district in which the lot is located. 
Section 1906 – Additional Lot Area and Dimension Regulations 
Any lot of record existing at the time this Ordinance or amendments thereto become effective: 
1. Which does not conform with the lot area or width requirements for the Zoning District 
in which it is located may be used for any use permitted in that Zoning District, if other 
applicable regulations of the Ordinance are met. 
2. Shall not be reduced in any manner below the lot area and width requirements of this 
Ordinance for the Zoning District in which it is located.  If a lot is already less than this 
minimum, such lot area or dimension shall not be further reduced. 
3. Shall not be reduced in any manner so as to cause the yards, lot coverage, open space, or 
lot area per dwelling unit except in conformance with this Ordinance.  No building 
permits shall be issued on any lot in violation of this paragraph.

d. For multi -use buildings, the usage requiring the smaller side setbacks shall be 
applied for the entirety of the building.  
2. The following limitations shall apply to the height of fences, walls, gateways, ornamental 
structures, hedges, shrubbery, and other fixtures on corner lots in all zoning districts 
where front yards are required. 
 
a. Barriers to clear, unobstructed vision at corners of intersecting streets shall be 
limited to a height not exceeding two feet (2’) above the elevation of the nearest 
street for a distance of twenty-five feet (25’) along each adjoining lot line, measured 
from the intersecting corner.
