Section 1909 – Administrative Waivers 
The Director or designee may, in their sole discretion, grant an Administrative Waiver of up to 
fifteen percent (15%) from any dimensional requirement(s) in this Ordinance including lot area, 
lot width, lot coverage, setback, building height, and other requirements stated in feet or square 
feet in circumstances where strict compliance would not be desirable or feasible. Requests for 
Administrative Waivers shall be made in writing and shall state why strict compliance is not 
desirable or feasible.  If a Waiver is granted, it shall be in writing and shall be recorded with the 
Navajo County Recorder’s Office. 
Section 1910 – Temporary Buildings/Uses  
Temporary Use Permits (TUP) may be permitted for the following uses, subject to obtaining a TUP 
from the Director or designee: 
1. Construction related buildings and uses, subject to the following conditions: 
 
a. Temporary buildings, Manufactured Homes and Recreational Vehicles (RV) used 
in conjunction with construction work may be permitted only during the period of 
construction. 
 
i. The duration of the TUP shall not be longer than one (1) year from the date 
of approval. The permit may be renewed for up to two (2) additional one -
year periods if the property owner submits satisfactory evidence of the need 
for renewal. 
ii. Unless renewed, the temporary building, Manufactured Home, or RV shall 
be removed from the site upon expiration of the permit, within ten (10) 
days after the completion of construction, or upon the granting of a 
Certificate of Occupancy, whichever comes first. 
iii. Temporary placement of an RV shall be subject to the provisions of Article 
14. No Temporary RV Permit (TRV) shall be required if a TUP has been 
issued. 
b. Temporary construction uses (such as the cutting and storage of lumber, materials, 
and equipment) related to construction may be permitted only during the period of 
construction. 
i.  The duration of the TUP shall not be longer than one (1) year from the date 
of approval. The permit may be renewed for up to two (2) additional one -
year periods if the property owner submits satisfactory evidence of the need 
for renewal. 
ii. Unless renewed, the temporary use shall cease upon expiration of the 
permit, within ten (10) days after the completion of construction, or upon 
the granting of a Certificate of Occupancy, whichever comes first.

<!-- page 811 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   82 
 
2. Real estate offices for the sale of subdivision lots.  
a. Temporary real estate offices for the sale of lots in a subdivision for which a final 
plat has been approved by the Board of Supervisors (BOS), subject to the following 
conditions: 
i. The office shall be located on the property being subdivided and shall be 
used solely for the sale of these lots. 
ii. The office shall comply with the height, setback, intensity of use, utility 
(including sewer) and parking regulations for the zoning district in which it 
is located. 
iii. The duration of the Temporary Use Permit shall not exceed two  (2) years 
from the date of approval, but the permit may be renewed for one (1) or 
more additional periods of not more than one  (1) year each if the property 
owner submits to the Director satisfactory evidence of the need for renewal 
(such as evidence that lots remain unsold). 
Section 1911 – Special Events 
This section applies to the short-term uses listed herein. If this section prescribes regulations more 
restrictive than the zone in which the use will be located, the provisions of this section shall apply. 
1. Uses for which a Special Event Permit (SEP) may be issued. All time requirements are one 
(1) time each calendar year for a specified number of consecutive days unless specifically 
stated otherwise. Only one (1) SEP may be issued for a parcel at any one time in a given 
year, except as noted below. Permits shall not have overlapping time frames. 
 
a. Outdoor special events, including: 
 
i. Transient amusement activities (carnivals, circuses and similar events). 
 
ii. Temporary faith-based assemblies (including tent revivals), and seasonal 
festivals. 
 
iii. Outdoor sales events (sidewalk and parking lot sales, auctions, and similar 
events). 
 
iv. Outdoor art and craft shows and exhibits. Such events shall be limited to a 
maximum of two (2) times per year, not to exceed five (5) days per event. 
 
b. Christmas tree sales lots, not to exceed sixty ( 60) days of site occupation and 
operation per year. 
 
c. Political campaign offices, not to exceed sixty ( 60) continuous days of site 
occupation and operation.

<!-- page 812 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   83 
 
d. Religious, patriotic, historic or similar displays or exhibits within yards, parking 
areas or landscaped areas, not to exceed thirty (30) days of display in any one-year 
period for each exhibit. No permit shall be required for a display or exhibit created 
by a homeowner or a religious, charitable, or educational organization on the 
homeowner’s or organization’s own property for the purpose of commemorating a 
traditional holiday or historical event. 
 
e. Stands for the sale of jewelry, furs, rugs and household items, not to exceed thirty 
(30) days per year. 
 
f. Stands for the sale of produce, not to exceed thirty (30) days per year. The 
provisions of this subsection do not apply to the sale of produce grown on the 
premises. 
 
g. Temporary retail food sales, not to exceed thirty (30) days per year. This shall 
include stands for food sales at one-day special events. No permit shall be required 
for the sale of "home-baked" items prepared by a homeowner or the members of a 
religious, charitable, or educational organization for sale on the homeowner’s or 
organization’s own property. 
 
h. Other short-term uses determined to by the Director to be similar to the foregoing. 
 
2. Special Event Permit.  All short -term uses listed in paragraph a shall require a SEP from 
the Director.  The application for a SEP shall be on a form approved by the Director and 
shall include: 
 
a. A detailed description of the proposed use. 
 
b. A site plan describing the location of the proposed use on the subject property. 
 
c. A statement of the date(s) on which the use will take place. 
 
d. The proposed daily hours of operation for the use. 
 
e. Written authorization from the owner of the property on which the use will be 
located. 
 
3. Fees.  The fee for a Special Event Permit shall be in accordance with a schedule of fees 
adopted by the Board of Supervisors. 
 
4. Bonds. The Director may require a cash bond not to exceed five -thousand dollars 
($5,000.00) to defray the cost of cleaning up the site if the permittee leaves it in an 
unsatisfactory condition.  Any such bond shall be immediately refunded to the permittee 
upon the cessation of the use, if the site is in satisfactory condition.

<!-- page 813 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   84 
 
5. Performance Standards.  Approval of a SEP shall be conditioned upon the permittee’s 
compliance with the following performance standards and any additional conditions 
deemed necessary by the Director in order to reduce possible detrimental effects to 
surrounding properties and protect the public health, safety, and welfare. 
 
a. Noise. Noise shall not be generated by any use to the point of disturbing the peace, 
quiet or comfort of neighboring properties. 
 
b. Parking. Adequate parking areas (including accessible parking) are required in the 
vicinity of the event. Parking shall be provided on the same property as the event 
to the fullest extent possible. Public rights -of-way shall be kept open and 
traversable during the operating hours of the event, and the permit holder shall 
ensure that there is no unreasonable interference with public travel. 
 
c. Location. No permit shall be issued for a site where the use is deemed potentially 
hazardous to the public. This includes heavily congested or trafficked areas where 
the use may impede or inconvenience the public. No use shall be permitted in a 
public right-of-way. 
 
d. Sanitation. All requirements of the County Health Department and other health 
authorities shall be met. Adequate provisions for the disposal of solid waste and 
waste water are required for all uses. 
 
e. One freestanding or wall-mounted on-site sign, not exceeding six square feet (6 ft2) 
is permitted.  This sign shall be removed immediately upon expiration of the 
permit.  Off -premise signage, on private property, shall be allowed, subject to 
compliance with all applicable  provisions of Article 17. A diagram of the sign, 
indicating size and location must be submitted with the permit application.  No 
signage is permitted in any public right -of-way, unless approved by the Director 
and Navajo County Public Work s Department.  Additional on -site or off -site 
directional signage may be permitted at the discretion of the Director. 
 
f. Lighting. All lighting sources shall be aimed or shielded so that the direct 
illumination is confined to the property on which the use is located. The operation 
of searchlights or similar lighting sources is prohibited. 
 
g. Other permits. Any required Health Department or Sheriff's Office permits or 
licenses, etc., shall be obtained before the use commences. 
 
6. Restoration of Site After Use. The site shall be left free of debris, litter or any other 
unsightly evidence of the use upon completion or removal of the use and shall thereafter 
be used only in accordance with the applicable provisions of the zoning regulations.

<!-- page 814 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   85 
 
7. Notice. The Director may notify adjacent property owners of an application for a 
Temporary use Permit in any reasonable manner and may solicit their comments prior to 
issuance of the permit. The Director’s decisions as to whether the application warrants 
notice to adjoining property owners, and as to the manner of such notice, shall be final.

1. An application for a Special Use Permit, together with the applicable fee as established

Section 1 913 – Storage of Manufactured Homes, Mobile Homes, Recreational 
Vehicles (RVs), Aircraft, or Boats. 
Unless permitted under the regulations set forth elsewhere in this Zoning Ordinance, the location 
or storage of Manufactured Homes and Recreational Vehicles (RVs) outside of Manufactured 
Home Parks, RV Parks, and Manufactured Home Subdivisions, and the loc ation or storage of 
aircraft and boats shall be subject to the following:

carport, it shall not be placed in the front yard setback, except that placement for loading

(24) hours.

of a principal dwelling. 
Section 1914 – Prohibition Against Placement/Movement of Mobile Homes 20 Years 
Old or Older 
Notwithstanding any other provision of the Zoning Ordinance, from and after March 1, 2024, no 
Mobile Home 20 years old or older at the time of application for mobile home/manufactured home 
permit shall be located within the unincorporated area of Navajo County. This prohibition shall

manufactured during or prior to 1976. If a Mobile Home lawfully located in the unincorporat ed 
area of Navajo County as of March 1, 2024, is thereafter to be relocated to another location within 
the unincorporated area of Navajo County, the owner shall obtain rehabilitation verification and 
any relevant permits from the Navajo County Building Div ision prior to issuance of a Certificate 
of Occupancy (COO).

Section 1915 – Lots Divided by Zoning District Boundaries 
Whenever a lot of record existing on the effective date of this ordinance is divided by a zoning 
district boundary in such a manner that more than fifty percent (50%) of the lot (by area) is located 
in one zone, the lot may be developed as though the entire lot were in that zone. This section shall 
also apply to any lot of record which is divided by a change in zoning district boundaries after the 
effective date of this ordinance. 
Section 1916 – Group Homes 
Group Homes for the Disabled 
1. Purpose: The purpose of these regulations is to permit disabled persons, as defined by 
state and federal law, to reside in single -family residences in compliance with the Fair 
Housing Act and Arizona state law, while maintaining the residential character of 
neighborhoods. 
 
2. Applicability: 
 
a. Zoning Confirmation: Prior to registration, requests for zoning confirmation may 
be submitted to the Department to confirm the proposed location of the group 
home is permitted per this Section. 
 
b. Group Homes for the Disabled Serving Six (6) or Fewer Residents: Group Homes 
for the Disabled that treat six (6) or fewer persons are not governed by this Section 
and shall only be subject to the regulations of the Zoning District in which the 
Group Home is established, in the same manner as any other s ingle-family 
residence, per A.R.S. § 36-582. 
 
c. Additional Requirements of State Law: Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the State 
has adopted laws or rules for the regulation of a specific type of home, such as a 
Group Home for the Developmentally Disabled or an Assisted Living Home as 
defined by state statutes, then any such State law or rule shall apply in addition to 
the conditions listed herein and shall preempt any conflicting condition listed 
herein. 
 
3. Performance Standards: Group Homes for the Disabled shall be located, developed, and 
operated in compliance with the following standards: 
 
a. Separation: The minimum separation between group homes shall be 1,200 feet as 
prescribed by A.R.S. § 36-582, as measured by the closest property lines. 
 
b. Occupancy: The number of residents, excluding staff, shall not exceed 10. 
 
c. Exterior Appearance: There shall be no sign or other exterior indication of a group 
home visible from a street. 
 
d. Compliance with Building, Environmental Health, and Fire Safety Regulations: 
Group homes shall be required to comply with all relevant building, environmental

<!-- page 817 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   88 
 
health, and fire safety regulations. If a group home has one or more non -
ambulatory residents, building code requirements in addition to those applicable 
to group homes containing no non-ambulatory residents, shall apply. 
 
e. Licensing: Group homes shall comply with applicable licensing requirements. 
 
f. Parking: Any parking for the group homes shall be on-site. 
 
4. Permits and Administration: 
 
a. Property is considered a Group Home for the Disabled under this Ordinance after 
the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Department issues a Permit for a Group 
Home for the Disabled for that property. Only properties serving occupants who fit 
the definition of disabled under the Fair Housing Act are eligible for determination 
as a Group Home for the Disabled. 
 
b. In order to secure a permit for a group home for the disabled, an application must 
be submitted on the form prescribed by the Department. The application must 
include the following: 
 
i. A site plan. 
 
ii. A notarized statement, detailing qualifications. 
 
iii. Copies of applicable licenses. 
 
iv. Affidavit of compliance and other documentation indicating the property as 
a group home for the disabled. 
 
v. Any additional information, or plans, if deemed necessary. 
 
c. If standards are not met, the home shall be considered an institutional residence or 
other group home and shall be subject to the provisions of the Zoning Ordinance 
regulating such establishments.  Status as a Group Home for the Disabled is open 
to review by the Department and may be cancelled at any time, upon a 
determination by the Director that the property is no longer being used for a 
qualifying purpose or meeting standards laid forth in this Ordinance. 
Institutional Residences and Other Group Homes 
1. Purpose: The purpose of these regulations is to provide guidelines for permitting group 
homes which do not qualify as group homes for the disabled.

<!-- page 818 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   89 
 
2. Applicability: 
 
a. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the State has adopted laws or rules for the 
regulation of a specific type of group home as defined by State statutes, then any 
such State law or rule shall apply in addition to the conditions listed herein and 
shall preempt any conflicting condition listed herein. 
 
3. Performance Standards: Institutional Residences and Other Group Homes shall be 
located, developed, and operated in compliance with the following standards: 
 
a. Separation: The minimum separation between group homes shall be 1200 feet as 
measured by the closest property lines. These group homes shall also not be located 
within 1200 feet from any religious, educational, or childcare facilities. 
 
b. Zoning: Institutional Residences and Other Group Homes shall only be allowed in 
the R-2, R-3, and C-R zoning districts upon acquiring a Special Use Permit. 
 
c. Occupancy: Occupancy shall be regulated within the zoning districts as listed 
below: 
 
i. R-2 and R-3: One resident for every bedroom within the residence. 
 
ii. C-R: Up to two residents for every bedroom within the facility. 
 
d. Exterior Appearance: Within R-2 and R-3 zoning districts, there shall be no sign or 
exterior indication of a group home visible from the street. Within C -R zoning, 
signage and exterior shall comply with the regulations of the zoning district. For 
group hom es within the R -2 and R -3 zoning districts, a solid wall or fence 
acceptable to the Director of Planning and Development Services shall be required 
around any side and rear yards. 
 
e. Compliance with Building, Environmental Health, and Fire Safety Regulations: 
Group homes shall be required to comply with all relevant building, environmental 
health, and fire safety regulations. If a group home has one or more non -
ambulatory residents, bu ilding code requirements in addition to those applicable 
to group homes containing no non-ambulatory residents, shall apply. 
 
f. Licensing: Group Homes shall comply with applicable licensing requirements. 
 
g. Parking: Any parking  for the group homes shall be on site and comply with all 
parking standards. No parking will be allowed on any street or within any right-of-
way. 
 
4. Permits and Administration: 
 
a. Property is considered an Institutional Residence or Other Group Home if it is a 
facility for living, sleeping, and sanitation and may include facilities for eating and

<!-- page 819 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   90 
 
cooking for occupancy other than a family which does not qualify as a group home 
for the disabled. 
 
b. In order for an Institutional Residence or Other Group Home to be an allowed use, 
a Special Use Permit must be obtained. The application must include the following: 
 
i. A site plan. 
 
ii. A copy of the recorded deed or sales contract. 
 
iii. A project narrative, including: 
 
1) Benefits of the use to the area. 
 
2) An explanation of the proposed use. 
 
3) A schedule for development.  
 
4) Compatibility of the proposed use with adjacent uses and character of 
the area. 
 
5) Details of the operation (number of residents to be served, number of 
individuals employed on -site, rules and regulations for operation and 
for residents, resident/facility schedules, security procedures, etc.). 
 
iv. A notarized statement detailing qualifications. 
 
v. Copies of applicable licenses. 
 
vi. Any additional information or plans, if deemed necessary.

1. Performance Standards. Approval of Guest Houses shall require compliance with the

ii. RU-20 
iii. RU-10 
iv. RU-5

dwelling.

c. An estimate of the valuation of the proposed construction. 
 
d. Satisfactory evidence of the applicant’s ability and intention to proceed with 
construction in accordance with the plans within six (6) months after the Guest 
House Permit is granted.

a. Applicable Building, Environmental Quality, and Engineering Permits apply. 
Department review shall be conducted through the issuance of such permits.

Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   92 
 
Section 1918 – General Conditions Applicable to Landfills 
1. Landfills require submission and review through a Special Use Permit.  In addition, the 
following information must be provided: 
a. A listing of all applicable Federal, State, and Local regulations that govern the 
proposed use. 
 
b. A proposed “Health and Safety Plan”. 
 
c. The method(s) of land-filling proposed. 
 
d. The proposed hours of operation and delivery of waste shipments. 
 
2. The siting, establishment and operation of a landfill must comply with all applicable 
existing and future rules and regulations adopted by the Environmental Protection 
Agency (EPA) and the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), or their 
successor agencies, including the Aquifer Protection Permit Rules adopted by ADEQ and 
in effect at the time of the review of the application. As a prerequisite to approval of the 
application for this Special Use, the following conditions may be applied: 
 
a. That the Health and Safety Plan may be required to go beyond State and Federal 
requirements and include State and Federal or other recommendations for the 
handling of certain materials. 
 
b. That there is a plan for the future use of the property upon cessation of landfilling 
activities, and that such re-use plan of the property is not inconsistent with adopted 
long range plans for the area. 
 
c. That the plan includes the creation of an escrowed sinking fund or other financial 
assurance acceptable to Navajo County and/or ADEQ to finance the future use of 
the property, such system to be funded while the property is still being used for 
land-filling and to be established in annual increments roughly equivalent to the 
development phase for the use of the site. The funding system must begin at the 
time of the development of the landfill. A sinking fund must be escrowed at least 
annually with the first annual payment thereto beginning in the first fiscal year of 
land-filling operations. 
 
d. That the landfill is visually screened from adjacent property and provides a buffer 
zone for protection of adjacent properties. Site specific conditions such as 
topography, elevation, surrounding land use or screening on adjoining properties  
to mitigate the requirements for screening and buffer zones. 
 
e. The landfill site must be maintained in a neat condition and fencing must be 
installed where necessary to catch blowing material. Additional fencing may be 
required on a case -by-case basis to provide security around active waste disposal 
cells.

<!-- page 822 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   93 
 
f. Access roads and driveways to the site must be all-weather roads. Access roads must 
connect directly to an arterial highway and will not require the use of any "street, 
collector" (servicing residential areas), or "streets, residential" as defined in the 
Navajo County Subdivision Regulations in effect at the time of this amendment. 
 
g. Sanitary toilet facilities must be provided for employees at the landfill site. 
 
h. That the landfill operator provides a list of generators and/or copies of waste 
manifests as may be required by EPA or ADEQ, for all material disposed in the 
landfill. This list shall be provided to Navajo County on a semi-annual basis. 
 
i. Scavenging will not be allowed on the landfill site. 
 
j. That the applicant will notify the County of any changes requested or agreed to by 
ADEQ or the EPA, after the Special Use Permit has been granted. Such changes 
may require modification of the Special Use Permit as specified in this Article. 
 
k. That the applicant will file, with the County, a final copy of all permits issued for 
the landfill by ADEQ or the EPA. 
 
l. All landfills must have a "Notice of Landfill Use" recorded against the title of the 
land that identifies all lands to be used for land-filling purposes. A landfill site plan 
and restrictions, if any, against future uses may also be required to be recorded . 
These documents must be recorded by a date specified as a condition of approval. 
 
m. The Department may waive or modify any of the requirements listed above. 
 
3. Waste Classifications. 
 
a. "Class I" Waste is a hazardous waste as defined in 40 CFR 261 and amendments 
thereto. 
 
b. "Class II" Waste consists of or contains chemically or biologically decomposable 
material, but does not include Class I waste. Class II waste includes, but is not 
limited to, the following: municipal and industrial solid waste, dead animals, 
sewage sludge and agricultural wastes. 
 
c. "Class III" Waste consists of non -water soluble, non -decomposable inert solids. 
Class III waste includes, but is not limited to the following: construction and 
demolition wastes, such as earth, rock, concrete, asphalt paving fragments, inert 
plastics, plasterboard, and demolition material containing minor amounts of wood 
and metals, vehicle tires, industrial wastes such as clay products, glass inert slags, 
asbestos, inert tailings and inert rubber scrap.

<!-- page 823 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   94 
 
4. Landfill Classifications. 
 
a. Class I. Class I landfills may accept Class I waste as defined in this Section for 
disposal. Class II and III wastes may also be placed in Class I landfills at the 
discretion of the landfill operator, unless otherwise restricted by Navajo County or 
ADEQ. 
 
b. Class II. Class II landfills may accept Class II waste as defined  in this Section for 
disposal. Class II landfills may accept Class III wastes, at the discretion of the 
landfill operator, unless otherwise restricted by Navajo County or ADEQ. Class II 
landfills SHALL NOT accept Class I wastes for disposal. 
 
c. Class III. Class III landfills may accept Class III waste as defined in this Section for 
disposal. Class I wastes SHALL NOT be placed in Class III landfills. Class III 
landfills may accept specific, pre -approved Class II wastes with prior written 
consent from the Board and ADEQ.

ARTICLE 20 – NON-CONFORMING USES 
Section 2001 – Continuing Existing Uses 
Any use of land, building, or structure, lawfully existing at the time of this Ordinance or 
amendments thereto become effective may be continued, even though such uses do not conform 
with the regulations of this Ordinance or amendment thereto for the Zoning District in which it is 
located.  
Section 2002 – Discontinuance of Non-Conforming Uses 
1. In the event that a non-conforming use of land, building, or structure is discontinued for 
a period of twelve (12) consecutive months, any future use thereof shall be in conformity 
with the regulations of this Ordinance.  
2. In the event that a non -conforming use of land, building, or structure is damaged to an 
extent of fifty percent (50%) or less of the appraised value, then it may be repaired and 
replaced, and the non -conforming use may be resumed, provided that restoration  is 
complete within a period of twelve (12) months.  
3. If the damage to a non-conforming use of land, building, or structure exceeds fifty percent 
(50%) of the appraised value, the structure is voluntarily razed, or is required by law to be 
razed, the use of land, building, or structure shall not be restored except in full conformity 
with the regulations of this Ordinance.  
4. Extent of damage shall be based on the ratio of the estimated cost of restoring land, 
building, or structure to its condition prior to such damage/partial destruction to the 
estimated cost of duplicating the entire land, building, or structure as it existe d prior to 
the damage.  Estimates for this purpose shall be reviewed and approved by the Director 
or Chief Building Official and shall be based on the minimum cost of construction in 
compliance with the adopted building codes.   
Section 2003 – Expansion of a Non-Conforming Use.  
1. A non -conforming use of land, building, or structure shall not be enlarged, expanded, 
reconstructed, or structurally altered unless such enlargement, extension, reconstruction, 
or structural alteration, and further use of such property conform with the reg ulations of 
this Ordinance.  
2. Non-conforming business uses may expand up to one hundred percent (100%) of the 
business area, pursuant to A.R.S. § 11 -812(B).  Proposed expansion to any use beyond 
the entitled one hundred percent (100%) is subject to all provisions of Special Use Permits 
and may be denied by the Board of Supervisors.  
3. For purposes of this section, “expansion” means the following: 
a. Construction of new buildings.  
b. Addition to existing buildings.  
c. Extension of a use into land originally zoned for the use, but not currently utilized 
by that use.

<!-- page 825 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   96 
 
4. For the purposes of this section, “expansion” does not mean the following: 
 
a. Any improvement required by Federal, State, or local environmental or health 
agency. 
b. Any increase in production volume utilizing existing equipment.  
c. Any extension of the use into an existing floor area originally designed for such 
extension, but not currently utilized by that use.  
5. No use established in violation of this Ordinance in its original or amended text may be 
considered as a conforming use or gain rights as a non -conforming use.  Further, the 
express intent of this Article does not waive the requirement for Building Permits  when 
expanding under the provisions of this section.  Under no circumstances do the provisions 
of this section permit the addition of new uses substantially different from the existing 
uses.

<!-- page 826 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   97 
 
ARTICLE 21 – ADMINISTRATION, VIOLATION, ENFORCEMENT, AND 
PENALTY 
Section 2101 – Duties  
The Director or designee, Code Enforcement Officers, Building Inspectors, and Navajo County 
Sheriff’s Office, as well as all other Navajo County officials charged with enforcement of the law 
may enforce provisions of this Ordinance and the Navajo County Bu ilding and Safety Codes.  As 
used herein, “Building and Safety Codes” means the codes adopted pursuant to A.R.S. § 11-861.  
The Director or designee, as appointed by the Board of Supervisors, shall be and shall have the 
authority of the “County Zoning Inspector,” as provided in A.R.S. § 11 -815. The Code 
Enforcement Officers and Building Inspectors, as appointed by the Board of Supervisors, shall be 
and shall have all authority of “Deputy Zoning Inspectors,” as provided in A.R.S. § 11-815.  
Section 2102 – Applications and Permits 
The Director and staff shall receive applications and issue permits required by this Ordinance and 
the Building and Safety Codes.  The Code Enforcement Officer and Building Inspectors shall 
examine premises where permits are to be issued, or were issued, a nd shall make inspections to 
ensure compliance with this Ordinance and the Building and Safety Codes.  
Section 2103 – Violations/Inspections 
A Code Enforcement Officer or Building Inspector may investigate alleged violations of this 
Ordinance and the Building and Safety Codes and are authorized to issue such notices of violation, 
citations, or complaints as may be required to enforce the provis ions of this Ordinance and the 
Building and Safety Codes. The provisions of this Ordinance and the Building and Safety Codes 
shall normally be enforced in response to citizen complaints, but complaints may also be initiated 
by the Board of Supervisors or D irector.  Citizen complaints may be made anonymously, and the 
names of citizen complainants shall not be disclosed without their prior consent.  A Code 
Enforcement Officer or Building Inspector, in performance of the duties imposed by law, shall 
have a right of reasonable access to all parcels of land  subject to this Ordinance and the Building 
and Safety Codes. 
Section 2104 – Other Violations; Unsightly, Unsanitary, or Hazardous Accumulations 
and Conditions 
In addition to violations of other Articles of this Ordinance, unsightly, unsanitary, or hazardous 
accumulations and conditions are prohibited and are considered violations of this Ordinance. 
Unsightly but sanitary and non -hazardous accumulations and condi tions are permitted in 
association with other businesses where such accumulations or conditions are necessary to the 
business (such as recycling facilities or construction sites).  Unsightly and hazardous 
accumulations shall be removed, enclosed in a permanent structure, or screened with conventional 
fencing materials in such a manner that they are no longer visible to neighbors or passers -by. 
Unsightly, unsanitary, or hazardous accumulations and conditions shall be determined at the 
discretion of the County Zoning Inspector and Deputy Zoning Inspectors.

<!-- page 827 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   98 
 
Section 2105 – Enforcement 
If a violation of this Ordinance or the Building and Safety Codes is found to exist, the Director or 
designee may, after reasonable efforts to achieve voluntary compliance have failed, consult with 
the County Attorney’s Office and initiate the appropriate enforcement action, pursuant to A.R.S. 
§§ 11-815 and 11-866. 
Section 2106 – Administrative Enforcement (Hearing Officer) 
1. Pursuant to A.R.S. §§ 11-815 and 11-866, the office of the Navajo County Zoning Hearing 
Officer is hereby established. 
2. One or more Zoning Hearing Officers shall be appointed by the Board of Supervisors. A 
Hearing Officer may be an employee of Navajo County but shall not be an employee of the 
Department.  
3. The Hearing Officer is authorized to hear and decide complaints alleging violations of this 
Ordinance, the Building and Safety Codes, and any other Navajo County ordinance or 
regulation.  
4. In the performance of their duties, the Hearing Officer is authorized to do the following: 
a. Administer oaths. 
b. Issue subpoenas and summonses for the appearance of persons before the Hearing 
Officer.  
c. Make any other orders necessary or appropriate for the determination and 
resolution of alleged violations.  
d. Upon determining that a violation exists, assess civil penalties as authorized by 
A.R.S. §§ 11-815 and 11-866, this Ordinance, or other applicable law. 
5. The rules and procedures for administrative enforcement shall be set forth in the Hearing 
Officer Rules and Procedures which have been adopted and are amended from time to 
time by resolution of the Board of Supervisors. 
Section 2107 – Penalties 
1. Penalties for violation of this Ordinance or Building and Safety Codes are outlined in 
A.R.S. §§ 11-815 and 11-866. 
2. Upon a determination by the Hearing Officer or by a civil or criminal court that a violation 
if this Ordinance or the Building and Safety Codes exists, no building permit, septic 
permit, floodplain use permit, or other permit or approval within the jurisdi ction of 
Navajo County, the Navajo County Flood Control District, or the Navajo County Public 
Health Services District shall be issued for the subject parcel until the violation has been 
cured or abated and all liabilities to the County have been resolved.

<!-- page 828 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   99 
 
ARTICLE 22 – NUISANCES AND ABATEMENT 
Section 2201 – Purpose and Authorization 
Pursuant to A.R.S. § 11-268, this Article codifies the ability of the Board of Supervisors to compel 
an owner, lessee, or occupant of buildings, grounds, or lots located within the unincorporated 
areas of Navajo County to remove rubbish, trash, weeds, filth, debris, or dilapidated buildings that 
constitute a hazard to public health and safety from buildings, grounds, lots, contiguous sidewalks, 
streets, and alleys. This article prescribes: 
1. Procedure for notice and appeal,  
2. Provides for the removal, abatement, or injunction thereof by the County and the 
assessment of the costs thereof as a lien against the property in the event of non -
compliance 
3. Prescribes a penalty for the placement of such materials on the property of another.  
SECTION 2202 – Removal of Public Nuisance by Owner, Lessee, or Occupant; 
Removal by County; Assessment of Costs; Recordation and Priority of Lien. 
1. Duty to Remove: The Owner, Lessee, or Occupant shall remove or otherwise abate a 
Public Nuisance located thereon within thirty (30) calendar days after service of a Notice 
to Abate or Enjoin, as provided herein.  
2. Notice to Abate or Enjoin:  The Notice to Abate or Enjoin shall be served by the County 
Attorney on behalf of the Board not less than thirty (30) calendar days before the date for 
compliance and shall include the estimated cost of removal if the Owner, Lessee, or 
Occupant does not comply.  The estimated cost of removal may be provided by a qualified 
contractor or may be a good faith estimate by the Department initiating the Notice to 
Abate. 
3. Service of Notice to Abate or Enjoin:  The Notice to Abate or Enjoin shall either be 
personally served or mailed by certified mail to the Owner, Lessee, and Occupant at their 
last known address, or the address to which the tax bill for the property was last mailed.  
If the Owner does not resid e on the property, a duplicate notice shall also be sent to the 
Owner at their last known address.  The Notice to Abate or Enjoin shall also be served or 
mailed by certified mail to any Lienholder having a Lien against the Real Property.  Failure 
or refusal to claim a notice within the time allowed by the postal authorities shall be 
deemed to constitute receipt by the addressee. 
4. Appeal of Notice to Abate or Enjoin: Any person receiving a Notice to Abate or Enjoin or 
otherwise having an interest in the Real Property may appeal to the Board as follows: 
a. Notice of Appeal: A written Notice of Appeal shall be filed with the Clerk of the 
Board within fifteen (15) days after the Notice to Abate or Enjoin was personally 
served or actually received by mail (as evidenced by the certified mail receipt or 
postal notice of refusal).  
b. Contents of Notice of Appeal: The Notice of Appeal shall state in reasonable detail 
why the appellant should not be required to comply with the Notice to Abate or 
Enjoin.  
c. Hearing on Appeal: Upon receipt of the Notice of Appeal, the Board shall place the 
matter on the agenda for its next regular meeting.  The Department which initiated 
the Notice to Abate or Enjoin shall appear and present evidence as to the existence

<!-- page 829 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   100 
 
of the Public Nuisance.  The appellant may present evidence as to the existence of 
the Public Nuisance.  The appellant may present evidence controverting the 
existence of the Public Nuisance.  The hearing shall be informal and without regard 
to the rules of procedure or evidence governing court proceedings.  The Board shall 
hear and decide the appeal, and its decision shall be final.  The appeal shall be 
sustained unless the Board upholds the Notice to Abate or Enjoin by majority vote. 
d. Extension of Time for Compliance: If the Board’s decision is adverse to the 
appellant, the date for compliance set forth in the Notice to Abate or Enjoin shall 
be extended by the number of days elapsing between the filing of the Notice of 
Appeal and the rendering of the Board’s decision.  
5. Removal by Board: If the Owner, Lessee, Occupant, or Lienholder fails to remove or 
otherwise abate the Public Nuisance within thirty (30) calendar days (or such extension 
thereof as may follow or be granted in writing by the County Attorney or the Board), The 
Board may, at the expense of the Owner, Lessee, or Occupant by majority vote, remove or 
abate the Public Nuisance or cause it to be removed, abated, or enjoined.  
a. Cost of Removal: The cost of removal, abatement, or injunction shall be the actual 
cost of removal or abatement, including the additional inspection and other 
incidental costs in connection with the removal or abatement and associated legal 
costs.  
b. Dilapidated Buildings: Before the removal of a Dilapidated Building, the Board 
shall consult with the state historic preservation officer to determine if the building 
may be of historical value.  Upon the removal of a Dilapidated Building, the County 
Assessor shall adjust the valuation of the Real Property on the property assessment 
tax roll from the date of removal.  
c. Assessment: Upon the removal, abatement, or injunction of the Public Nuisance, 
the Cost of Removal, per paragraph 5a shall be an Assessment against the Real 
Property on which the Public Nuisance was located.  The form of the Assessment 
(setting forth facts  supporting it, as well as the date and amount and a legal 
description of the Real Property) shall be approved and signed by the County 
Attorney, or designee.  
d. Notice of Assessment: A Notice of Assessment shall be served in the same manner 
as the Notice to Abate or Enjoin.  The Notice of Assessment may be appealed in the 
same manner as the Notice to Abate or Enjoin, but the issue shall be limited to the 
amount of the Assessment.  An appeal shall extend the time for payment, in the 
same manner as set forth in paragraph 4d.  
e. Recordation of Assessment: If the Owner, Lessee, or Occupant fails to pay the 
Assessment within thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Abate or 
Enjoin (or any extension as may follow an appeal or be granted in writing by the 
County Attorn ey or the Board), the Assessment shall be delinquent and may be 
recorded in the office of the Navajo County Recorder.  The Assessment shall be a 
lien against the Real Property from and after the date of recordation and shall 
accrue interest at the statutor y judgment rate until paid.  The Lien of the 
Assessment shall be prior and superior to all other liens, obligations, or 
encumbrances against the Real Property, except liens for general taxes and prior 
recorded mortgages.  
f. Foreclosure: The Board may, but shall not be obligated to, by majority vote, bring 
an action to enforce  the Assessment lien in the Navajo County Superior Court at 
any time after the Assessment becomes delinquent in accordance with Paragraph 
5g.  A sale of Real Property to satisfy the assessment shall be made on judgment of 
foreclosure and order of sale.  The recorded Assessment is prima facie evidence of

<!-- page 830 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   101 
 
the truth of all matters recited therein and of the regularity of all proceedings before 
the recordation thereof.  
g. Assessment Payment: Assessments that are imposed under this Article run against 
the property until they are paid and are due and payable in equal annual 
installments, as prescribed by A.R.S. § 11 -268(E).  If any installment is not paid 
when due and payable, the Assessment shall be deemed delinquent and subject to 
foreclosure.  
h. No Bar to Subsequent Assessments: A prior Assessment under this Ordinance is no 
bar to a subsequent Assessment, and any number of liens on the same Real may be 
enforced in the same action.  
Section 2203 – Placing Rubbish, Trash, Filth, or Debris on Property of Another; 
Penalty; Assessment 
1. Placing Rubbish, Trash, Filth, or Debris on Property of Another is Prohibited: Any person 
who places rubbish, trash, filth, or debris on any Real Property not owned by or under the 
control of said person is guilty of a Class 1 Misdemeanor.  
2. Liability for Costs: In addition to any fine which may be imposed pursuant to Paragraph 
1, the person who places rubbish, trash, filth, or debris on any Real Property not owned 
by or under the control of said person shall be liable for all costs which may assessed for 
the removal of the rubbish, trash, filth, or debris, pursuant to Section 2202.  
Section 2204 – Non-Exclusive Remedy 
The remedies provided for in this Ordinance shall be in addition to an and all other remedies, civil 
or criminal, available to Navajo County pursuant to statute or common law, specifically including 
those set forth in A.R.S. §§ 13-2908, 36 -602, and 49 -143 and the Uniform Code for the 
Abatement of Dangerous Buildings.

<!-- page 831 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   102 
 
ARTICLE 23 – DEFINITIONS 
1. Accessory Building: Shall mean an Accessory Building as defined in A.R.S. 41-2142 and the 
related regulations of the State Office of Manufactured Housing, as amended from time 
to time. 
2. Adjoining Property: Any parcels of land identified by a separate Assessor Parcel Number 
and that either physically touch the subject parcel or would touch if not separated by a 
dedicated right-of-way. 
3. Airport: A landing area used regularly by aircraft for receiving or discharging passengers or 
cargo. 
a. Heliport: a landing area solely for the use of helicopters.  A heliport may include 
one or more helipads. 
b. Landing Area: any locality, either land or water, including airports, and landing 
fields, which is used or intended to be used for the landing and take-off of aircraft, 
or for receiving or discharging passengers or cargo. 
c. Landing Area Boundary: the outer limit of the land or water of a landing area. 
4. Alley: A passage or way open to public travel which generally allows a secondary means of 
vehicular access to abutting lots and is not intended for general traffic circulation. 
5. Alley Line: The boundary which separates the right-of-way of an alley from the abutting 
property. 
6. Alternative Tower Structure: Vertical components not generally designed for use as antenna 
support structures including, but not limited to, structures such as church steeples, 
ballpark light poles, and water towers. 
7. Antenna: Any exterior device for transmitting and receiving wireless communication 
mounted on a tower, alternative tower structure, building, or structure and used for 
transmitting and receiving wireless communication for a fee to more than one (1) 
customer at one time. 
8. Antenna, attached: An antenna mounted on the exterior of an existing building, silo, 
smokestack, water tower, utility or power pole, existing wireless communication tower, 
or an alternative support structure. 
9. Antenna, concealed: An antenna with a support structure that screens or camouflages the 
presence of antennas and/or towers from public view, in a manner appropriate to the site’s 
context and surrounding environment. 
10. Area of Jurisdiction: The unincorporated areas of Navajo County that are not within the 
boundary of a reservation, nor within the corporate limits of any municipality. 
11. Basement: That portion of a building between the floor and ceiling which is wholly or 
partly below grade and having more than one-half of its height below grade. 
12. Board of Supervisors: The Board of Supervisors of Navajo County.

<!-- page 832 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   103 
 
13. Boarding House: A building where, for compensation and by prearrangement for 
definitive periods, meals, or lodgings and meals, are provided for three (3) or more 
persons, but not exceeding twenty (20) persons.  
14. Building: A structure located on Real Property, enclosed within exterior walls, built, 
erected, and framed of a combination of materials, whether portable or fixed, having a 
roof, to form a structure for the shelter of persons, animals, or property. 
15. Building Area: The portion of a lot which is within the envelope formed by the required 
yards. See “Yard”.  
16. Building, Community: A public building designed or used for community activities of an 
educational, recreational, or public service nature. 
17. Building Height: The vertical distance from grade to the highest point of the coping of a 
flat roof, to the deck line of a mansard roof, or the mean roof height of the highest gable, 
hip, or gambrel roof.  
18. Building, Principal: a building in which the principal use of the lot on which the building 
is located is conducted.  In a residential zoning district any dwelling is deemed to be the 
principal building on the lot on which it is situated. 
19. Building Wall: The entire surface area, including windows and doors, of an exterior wall 
of a building. 
20. Canopy: a permanent structure other than an awning made of cloth, metal, or other 
material attached or unattached to a building for the purpose of providing shelter to 
patrons or automobiles or as a decorative feature on a building wall.  A canopy is not a  
completely enclosed structure. 
21. Carport: A roofed structure with two (2) or more open sides, under which a vehicle may 
be driven/stored. 
22. Cellar: That portion of a building between floor and ceiling which is partly below and partly 
above grade, but so located that the vertical distance from grade to floor below is greater 
than the vertical distance from grade to ceiling. 
23. Certification: A written statement of the fact to be certified, made under oath by the 
applicant or licensed professional working for the applicant and notarized. 
24. Church: A building, together with its accessory buildings and use, where people regularly 
assemble for religious purposes and related social events and which building, together 
with its accessory buildings and uses, is maintained and controlled by a religi ous body 
organized to sustain religious ceremonies and purposes. For the purpose of this definition, 
a "church" shall be required to maintain a tax-exempt status per ARS 42-11109. 
25. Collocation: Use by two (2) or more wireless communication providers located on the same 
tower or alternative tower structure. 
26. Commercial Coverage: A single FCC licensee’s network of wireless communications 
facilities providing a level of service to all areas of the community which, when fully 
developed, will permit viable commercial operation.

<!-- page 833 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   104 
 
27. Copy: any words, letters, numbers, figures, characters, symbols, logos, or insignia that are 
used on a sign display surface area. 
28. Commission: The Planning and Zoning Commission of Navajo County.  
29. Contractor’s Yard: A portion of a lot or parcel upon which a construction contractor 
maintains its principal office or a permanent business office. Designation of the lot or 
parcel as a contractor’s storage yard would allow this area to be sued to store and maintain 
construction equipment and other materials customarily used in the trade carried on by 
the construction contractor. If permitted to be used in this manner, the entire lot or parcel 
would then be classified as a “contractor’s yard” and will be re quired to conform to all 
applicable zoning district standards and other legislative regulations.  
30. Corral: A pen or enclosure for confining animals.  
31. County: The unincorporated areas of Navajo County. 
32. Dilapidated Building: Any building in such disrepair, or damaged to such an extent, that 
its strength or stability is substantially less than a new building, or is likely to burn or 
collapse, and the condition of which endangers the life, health, safety, o r property of the 
public.  
33. Direct Illumination: means illumination resulting from light emitted directly from a lamp, 
luminaire or reflector, not light diffused through translucent signs or reflected from other 
surfaces such as the ground or building faces. 
34. Director: The Director of the Navajo County Planning and Development Services 
Department, or his or her designee.  
35. Dwelling: A building, or portion thereof, for human habitation, which shall not include a 
trailer or other mobile living unit or hotel, dormitory, hospital or rooming house.  
36. Dwelling Group: A group of two or more single-family or multi-family dwellings occupying 
a parcel of land in one ownership and having a yard in common, but not including motels.  
37. Dwelling Multiple: A building, or portion thereof, designed exclusively for occupancy by 
three or more families living independently of each other in individual dwelling units.  
38. Dwelling, Single-Family: A building designed for occupancy by one (1) family.  
39. Dwelling, Duplex: A building containing two dwelling units, each of which has direct 
access to the outside.  
40.  Dwelling Unit: One or more habitable rooms which are occupied, or which are intended 
or designed to be occupied as a residence by one family, with facilities for living, sleeping,

41. Factory-Built Building: Shall mean a Factory-Built Building as defined in A.R.S. 41-2142 
and the related regulations of the State Office of Manufactured Housing, as amended from 
time to time. 
42. Family: An individual, or two (2) or more persons related by blood, marriage, or adoption, 
or other legal relationship including any live -in domestic help, living together as a single

<!-- page 834 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   105 
 
housekeeping unit in a dwelling unit, or a group of not more than five (5) adults, who need 
not be related, living together as a single housekeeping unit in a dwelling unit. 
43. Farm:  An area of not less than two (2) contiguous acres which is used for the commercial 
production of farm crops such as vegetable, fruit trees, grain and other crops and their 
storage on the area, as well as the raising thereon of farm poultry and farm animals, such

44. Farm Product Sales: seasonal sale of farm products raised on the premises or where

45.  Feedlot, Commercial: Establishments engaged in the fattening, raising, or breeding of

46. Floor Area: The sum of the square footage of all of the floors of a structure or building, e.g. 
the sum of the horizontal areas of each floor of a building, measured from the interior 
faces of the exterior walls or from the centerline of walls separating t wo buildings. The 
floor area measurement is exclusive of areas of basements, unfinished attics, attached 
garages or space used for off -street parking or loading, breezeways, enclosed and 
unenclosed porches, elevator or stair bulkheads, and accessory structures.  
47. Fully Shielded Fixture: means that fixtures are shielded in such a manner that light rays 
emitted by the fixture, either directly from the lamp or indirectly from the fixture, are

48. Garage, Private: A portion of a principal building, or separate, accessory building,

sides. 
49. Garage, Public: A building or portion thereof, other than a private garage, designed or

50. Gas Station: Any commercial building or structure, premises, or other place used to supply 
motor fuels, lubricants, tires, batteries, and other small accessories to motor vehicles, and

conjunction with a service station.  
51. Grade: The average of the finished ground level at the midpoint of each wall of a building. 
In case walls are parallel to and within five feet of a public sidewalk, said ground level 
shall be measured at the sidewalk. 
52. Grade, sign: the height of the top of the curb, or if no curb exists, the height of the edge of 
pavement in the lane of travel adjacent to the sign.

<!-- page 835 -->
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   106 
 
53. Group Home for the Disabled: a residential facility that is licensed or authorized by a 
governmental authority that provides care, support, and supervision to people with

54. Grounds: Any private or public land, vacant or improved (Needed?)  
55. Guest: Any transient person who occupies a room for sleeping purposes.

Dear Navajo County Staff and Supervisors, 
AES would like to  thank County Staff and Supervisors for organizing multiple forums for public 
engagement as well as soliciting industry feedback on the proposed  Renewable Energy Ordinance. As a 
developer, owner, and operator of energy infrastructure with nearly 1,000 MWs of wind energy operating 
and under construction in Coconino and Navajo Counties, AES values the input of our host communities 
and neighbors. This letter serves to provide AES’s written input on potential ordinance revisions discussed 
during the Work Session on February 11, 2025 and during the Renewable Energy Listening Sessions hosted 
the week of March 24, 2025 in Show Low, Heber, and Joseph City.   
Proposed Existing Setback Increases   
During these sessions, Staff presented multiple setback increases for public consideration, including: i) an 
increase in the turbine distance from legal residences from ½ -mile to 1 -mile; and ii) an increase in the 
turbine distance from non-participating private lands (for parcels greater than 2.5 acres) from ¼ -mile to 
½-mile. Navajo County’s existing ordinance property boundary setback s and noise limits are  the most 
restrictive in Arizona. The proposed increase in setbacks from legal residences would make them the most 
restrictive in the state as well.  
These impacts would significantly limit participating  landowners’ ability to maximize the value of their 
land, while potentially decreasing the size of wind projects and thus degrade economic benefits, including 
lease payments and property tax revenues. If implemented at the currently permitted and under 
construction West Camp  Wind Farm in Navajo County, the proposed setback increases would have 
encumbered an additional  6,759 acres of leased private property from turbine siting, effectively  
eliminating 16% of the turbines currently being constructed.  
Proposed New Setbacks   
During the public listening sessions, Staff discussed potential  2-mile or 5 -mile setbacks from municipal 
boundaries and Forest Service property . This would establish a uniquely challenging precedent for 
development whereby future municipal incorporation could impede unpermitted projects . There is 
currently no similar setback requirement in the state of Arizona.  Additional consultation with 
municipalities may yield a more case-by-case approach instead of implementing a common setback from 
incorporated areas across the County. 
With respect to the potential  Forest Service setback, we would encourage the County to consider the 
actual natural resources that this proposed setback attempts to protect and avoid. We believe a case-by-
case analysis of each project on a resource-specific basis would be more appropriate, in accordance with 
the recommended approach of wildlife agencies. Wind energy projects are required to  consult with the

<!-- page 917 -->
The AES Corporation   |   282 Century Pl #2000   |   Louisville, CO 80027
Arizona Game and Fish Department and  the United States Fish and Wildlife Service throughout 
development, during which site-specific setbacks from natural resources  are often recommended . It 
should also be noted that a Forest Service  setback would effectively prohibit siting wind turbines on 
federal land in Navajo County.  Wind energy sited on private, state, and federal land in the western United 
States where compatible land uses exist can be a robust form of economic development and revenue 
generation for state and federal agencies. 
Overall Perspective 
AES submits that the existing Navajo County Wind E nergy Ordinance complies with key principles of 
Arizona State Law (see Appendix 1). The existing ordinance is a thoughtful, stringent, well -crafted 
regulation that lawfully balances the interests of landowners and neighboring properties alike. 
When reviewing other local laws around the state and the country, Navajo County ’s wind energy 
ordinance ensures that developers build projects in a manner that limits their impact on the surrounding 
community. These restrictions are based on significant scientific research, and our team believes that 
additional setbacks and restrictions would not yield the desired effect of balancing renewable energy 
economic development while protecting environmental, wildlife, visual, noise,  and other community 
impacts. Additional restrictions would make the development of wind farms in Navajo County incredibly 
challenging while effectively encumbering the right of private, state, and federal agencies to host wind 
energy as a compatible land use that provide s supplemental, forecastable revenue, while spurring jobs 
and economic growth in the broader Navajo County community.   
During the listening sessions, there were numerous local business owners that spoke of the tangible, 
positive impacts they have felt from wind energy  – these ranged from concrete and aggregate suppliers 
to construction equipment rental centers, to residents and other contractors living and working in Navajo 
County. Furthermore, numerous longstanding landowners and local families spoke in support of wind 
energy as a means of continuing their long-term land stewardship and supplementing their existing land 
uses.   
AES looks forward to proposing future renewable energy projects which align with Staff’s proposed 
performance criteria to  bring significant economic benefit to the County , while also delivering reliable, 
affordable energy to power Arizona’s growing economy and energy needs. AES can do this while 
respecting and maintaining the rural character and preserving the environmental resources that make 
Navajo County such a special place. We’re confident that land use policies and zoning ordinances, building 
off the incredible work already performed within Navajo County, can strike an appropriate balance in 
terms of addressing residents’ concerns, respecting landowners’ rights, and meeting the state’s needs for 
producing reliable and affordable energy in Arizona, for Arizona. 
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Appendix 1 - Key Legal Principles 
As Staff has recognized, private property rights are implicated by any proposed changes to the County’s 
ordinance. In Arizona, individual rights are paramount . See Arizona Constitution, Art. 2, §§ 1 and 2 (“A 
frequent recurrence to fundamental principles is essential to the security of individual rights and the 
perpetuity of free government” and “governments … are established to protect and maintain individual 
rights.”).  
A County can only regulate private property rights to the extent such powers have been expressly 
conferred by statute.  See, e.g., Robinson v. Lintz, 101 Ariz. 448, 450-451 (1966) (citing cases).  No implied 
powers exist because “Zoning Ordinances, being in derogation of common law property rights, will be 
strictly construed and any ambiguity or uncertainty decided in favor of property owners. ”  Id. at 451 
(quoting Kubby v. Hammond, 68 Ariz. 17 (1948). 
Even when the County has been given the power to regulate, restrictions cannot be imposed unless 
necessary to accomplish a substantial government purpose.   See Penn Central Transportation Co. v New 
Your City, 438 U.S. 104, 127 (1978).   Further, a use “restriction cannot be imposed if it does not bear a 
substantial relation to the public health, safety, morals, or general welfare.”  Nectow v. City of Cambridge, 
277 U.S. 183 (1928).

Section 1201 – Renewable Energy Generation Facilities 
1. Zoning Districts in which allowed
Renewable Energy Generation facilities are allowed only in the A -General, Rural, and 
Industrial Zoning Districts, subject to either securing a Special Use Permit, 
Development Agreement, or both, and to the applicable site development standards set 
forth herein.  The project application shall comply with the submittal application 
requirements of Navajo County for the particular project. 
This Article does not purport to regulate Renewable Energy Generation projects on 
state or federal land except insofar as state or federal agencies may require compliance 
with Navajo County zoning requirements as part of their own application processes. In 
the event of any inconsistency between any requirement of this Section and any 
requirement of state or federal law, now or in the future, the state or federal 
requirement shall control and this section shall be interpreted and applied consistently 
therewith. 
2. General Development Standards for Renewable Energy Generation Facilities
a. Conceptual and Pre-application Meetings. Because additional information may be
required for effective review, conceptual and pre -application meetings with a
representative from the Department are required.   The Authority Having
Jurisdiction for fire and the local responding fire agency are required to be notified
and invited to these meetings.  The level of detail and analysis necessary is
dependent on the type of project proposed, its location, and the currently available
information relevant to the proposal.
b. A minimum of on-site roadways shall be constructed and maintained in accordance
with IFC to support fire apparatus .  Temporary access roads and excess roadway
widths for initial equipment/facility installation shall be revegetated, using native
species plants and seeds, to a pre -project condition (to the extent reasonably
possible) after completion of installation as a condition of project approval.  The
applicant shall submit a plan of all proposed roads, temporary and permanent, for
review and approval by the Public Works Department prior to the issuance of any
grading or building permits.
c. Applicants shall record the condition of any County -maintained roadways,
following receipt of planned access to the project, within a reasonable time, prior
to commencement of construction operations.  Documentation of the roadways’
conditions shall be kep t by Navajo County and shared with the applicant.  A Road
Use Agreement shall be agreed upon by the County and applicant, and recorded in
the Navajo County Recorder’s Office, prior to any construction activities.

d. Electrical collector lines, which connect electricity generation devices to any 
substations, shall be placed underground except where (a) they cross sensitive 
biological or archaeological resources, such as canyons, wetlands, or sites eligible 
for the nati onal register, or rugged terrain that would prevent the use of 
underground trenching and technology, (b) project terrain is found to be 
unsuitable, as determined by the applicant and confirmed by the County Engineer, 
or (c) burying the lines would violate applicable laws or regulations.  In these cases, 
collector lines will be allowed above ground subject to approval by the Planning

phone requirements of buildings shall be placed in accordance with the utility’s 
easement requirements.

Uniform Fire Code and as required by the  Authority Having Jurisdiction for fire, 
as well as the local responding fire agency. 
 
f. All renewable energy projects shall require approval and improvements as 
requested by the Authority Having Jurisdiction for fire, as well as the local

iii. Wetland Delineation Report. 
 
iv. Citizen Participation Plan.

Services Department and County Attorney’s Office. The permit/agreement holder

The Board of Supervisors, upon the recommendation of the County Attorney and 
the Director, may approve variations from the requirements of this paragraph if 
warranted by the particular circumstances of a project. 
 
t. Preferred Criteria. Renewable Energy Generation facilities shall use the preferred 
facility type and location, where possible.  Site location and development of 
installations shall minimize negative impacts to the surrounding landscape and/or 
community.  Preferred criteria are intended to guide decisions about the location 
and siting of Renewable Energy Generation Facilities.  Preferred facility sites are 
as follows: 
 
i. A project site that has minimal visual impact. 
ii. A project site that uses or is near existing substations, transmission lines, 
or points of interconnection. 
iii. Project sites that are on previously disturbed land such as brownfield sites, 
mining sites, sites with low wildlife habitat and vegetation value, or with 
few cultural resources. 
iv. Project sites that allow multiple uses of the land, such as ranching, 
agricultural, and recreational uses.

viii. Projects that include community benefits.

aa.  Permit Suspension and Revocation

<!-- page 925 -->
Article 12 – Renewable Energy   Section 1201 – Renewable Energy Generation Facilities 
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   7 
 
i. Any SUP issued pursuant to this section may be suspended or revoked in 
whole or part by the Board of Supervisors for material non -compliance 
with the requirements of this section or the stipulations set forth in the 
SUP.  SUP shall be subject to suspension or revocation at a duly noticed 
public hearing only if the SUP holder has failed to cure the material non-
compliance after no less than thirty (30) days’ written notice of such non-
compliance from the Director. 
 
ii. If a Renewable Energy Generation facility becomes unsafe or inoperable, 
the SUP is likewise subject to suspension or revocation by the Board of 
Supervisors as follows: 
 
1) An “inoperable Renewable Energy Generation facility” is one that does 
not generate a significant amount of electricity for one-hundred eighty 
(180) consecutive days, unless such non -generation is due to an act of 
nature, declared emergency or other cause beyond the reasonable 
control of the SUP holder or unless the SUP holder demonstrates that 
modernization, rebuilding or repairs are in progress or are planned and 
will be diligently completed. 
 
2) An “unsafe Renewable Energy Generation facility” is one that has been 
found by a state or federal administrative agency or a court of competent 
jurisdiction to have materially violated applicable health or safety laws, 
unless the SUP holder demonstrates that measures to cure such 
violations are in progress or a re planned and will be diligently 
completed. 
 
3) Every unsafe or inoperable Renewable Energy Generation facility is 
hereby declared to be a public nuisance per se which shall be subject to 
abatement by all available legal and equitable remedies. 
 
4) Upon a complaint by the Director that a Renewable Energy Generation 
facility is inoperable or unsafe, the Board of Supervisors shall convene 
a public hearing at the earliest possible date after written notice to the 
SUP holder. Pending a final determination that the facility is inoperable 
or unsafe, the Board may suspend the SUP in whole or part or impose 
such conditions as may be appropriate to protect the public health, 
safety and welfare. Upon a final determination that the facility is 
inoperable or  unsafe, the Board may suspend or revoke the SUP in 
whole or part or impose such conditions as may be appropriate to 
protect the public health, safety and welfare. 
 
iii. No later than  thirty (30) days after the revocation or expiration of the 
SUP, the decommissioning plan required by this Section  shall be 
implemented and decommissioning shall proceed diligently to 
completion.

Section 1202 – Wind Energy Generation Facilities 
The following provisions shall be specific for the review of Wind Energy Generation Facilities: 
1. Audible sound limits:  
 
a. Audible noise due to project operations shall not exceed the greater of: (a) 45 dBA 
LAeq,10; or,  
 
b. The measured background, LA90,10 plus 5 dB, as measured at the exterior at any legal 
residence, school, library or hospital in existence at the time of approval of the SUP.  
 
2. If sound levels resulting from a proposed facility exceed the criteria specified above, a 
waiver may be granted after review and recommendation by the Planning and 
Development Services Department, provided that the following has been 
accomplished:  
 
a.  An irrevocable written consent (or sound waiver easement) has been obtained 
from each affected property owner, stating that the owner is aware of the proposed 
facility and the sound limitations imposed by this section, that consent is granted 
to allow sound levels to exceed the maximum limits specified herein, and that such 
consent will be memorialized in a notice recorded with the Navajo County Recorder 
to notify future owners of the affected property that sound levels may exceed the 
sound levels specifie d herein. The consent shall include a legal description of the 
affected property. A copy of each such consent on which the permit/agreement 
holder relies shall be submitted prior to approval of the permit/agreement. 
 
3. All wind turbine operations shall meet the operational low -frequency noise 
requirements applicable to wind turbines as specified in Noise Requirement 
Guidelines adopted, published and amended from time to time by the Board of 
Supervisors. 
 
4. Background and Compliance Testing: The requirements of subparagraph a above 
require that background (predevelopment) sound levels be properly assessed, that 
sound levels be forecast in advance of permit/agreement approval, and that, once a 
project commences operation, sound levels again be assessed as part of compliance -
period assessment. Before a permit/agreement is issued, the applicant’s independent 
consultant shall complete a sound evaluation by determining existing (pre -project) 
background sound levels  and forecasting ambient sound levels anticipated upon 
completion of the facility. The evaluation shall address facility aging and planned or 
probable modifications. If the project is permitted and constructed, when it is in 
operation the permit/agreement holder’s independent consultant shall complete a 
compliance-period sound evaluation. Background and post -construction compliance 
sound measurements shall comply with Noise Requirement Guidelines adopted, 
published and amended from time to time by the Board of Supervisors. If there is any 
conflict between the requirements of this ordinance and the requirements of such 
guidelines, the more stringent requirement(s) shall control. For phased/staged 
development, background sound levels shall be determined before the initial phase of

<!-- page 927 -->
Article 12 – Renewable Energy            Section 1202 – Wind Energy Generation Facilities 
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance   9 
 
the project. For a situation in which multiple developments by the same or multiple 
developers are expected in an area, the same applies. 
 
5. During the first three months of facility operation and more specifically during a 
period of normal full production operations, the SUP holder shall verify compliance 
with subparagraph a above utilizing an independent consultant. If operational sound 
is found to exceed the limits specified in subparagraph a above, the SUP holder shall 
institute remedies to achieve compliance with the applicable limits, or submit a 
consent from each owner of an affected property in accordance with subparagraph b 
above. Durin g the remedy period the SUP holder shall identify and remove from 
service the equipment responsible for the excessive sound until the problem can be 
cured or mitigated. Navajo County staff may require additional compliance testing 
when deemed appropriate. 
 
6. Plans for determining background sound levels and for modeling/simulation shall be 
submitted by the applicant for the Planning and Development Services Department’s 
review and approval in advance of the work. 
 
7. Setbacks. The minimum safety setback distance, location and spacing requirements 
for Wind Energy Generation facilities shall be as follows. As used herein, “total tower 
height” means the height from grade to the top of the structure, including the 
uppermost extension of any blade (i.e., “straight up”). 
 
a. Wind towers shall be placed in accordance with the greater of the applicable 
setback and location requirements set forth in paragraphs A, B, and C below:  
 
i.  Such that the sound standards established in subparagraph b of this 
Section will not be exceeded.  
 
ii. Setbacks related to areas outside the project boundary:  
 
1) Setback to existing residence: Individual wind towers shall be placed 
within the project boundary at least ½ -mile (2,640 feet) from an 
existing residence that is located outside of the project boundary.  
 
2) Setback to adjacent privately -owned land that is not zoned Industrial 
(I-1 or I-2):  
 
a) Parcels greater than 2.5 acres in size: Individual wind towers 
shall be placed within the project boundary at least ¼ -mile 
(1,320 feet) or 150% of the total tower height (whichever is 
greater) from the common property line with such parcels.  
 
b) Parcels 2.5 acres or smaller in size: Individual wind towers shall 
be placed within the project boundary at least ½ -mile (2,640 
feet) or 150% of the total tower height (whichever is greater) 
from the common property line with such parcels.

Article 12 – Renewable Energy            Section 1202 – Wind Energy Generation Facilities

Adjacent parcel sizes as set forth in paragraphs 1-2 above shall 
be determined as of the effective date of this Section.  
 
c) All other adjacent land not included in one of the foregoing 
categories: Individual wind towers shall be placed at least 
1.1 times (110%) the total tower height from the project 
boundary. 
 
iii. Setbacks related to areas within or outside the project boundary:  
 
1. Roadway (public or publicly-maintained): Individual wind towers shall be set back from 
any public or publicly-maintained roadway (as measured to the nearest edge of the right-
of-way) at least ¼-mile (1,320 feet).  
 
2. Railways, utility lines, interior phase lines and structures: Individual wind towers shall be

a. The minimum setbacks from the project boundary for all non -tower uses and

towers, maintenance buildings, operations buildings, transformers, etc.) shall 
conform to the setback requi rements for the Zoning District in which the use or

b. A reduction in the setback requirements set forth above in accordance with any or

i. The project shares a common property line with another approved Wind

ii. An irrevocable written consent from an affected property owner has been

will be memorialized in a notice recorded with the Navajo County

iii. An adjacent property owner who is also pursuing the development of a

iv. The parcel on which the project is located and an adjacent parcel are held

8. Wind Energy Generation projects shall comply with applicable Federal Aviation

minimum required by FAA regulations or other public safety considerations. The use of 
low-intensity, red pulsating/blinking lighting is preferred so long as consistent with FAA

unless specifically required by the FAA. All lighting shall be in compliance with the Navajo

9. Wind Energy Generation facility projects shall comply with applicable Federal

communications interference generated by the project). No interference with public 
communication systems shall be allowed. 
 
10. Towers, generator housings, hubs and blades shall be painted a non -reflective,
